stotra.description: The 1000 names of Lord Vishnu composed by Sage Vyasa, narrated by Bhishma Pitamaha.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
शुक्लाम्बरधरं विष्णुं शशिवर्णं चतुर्भुजम् ।
प्रसन्नवदनं ध्यायेत् सर्वविघ्नोपशान्तये ॥१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: शुक्लाम्बरधरं विष्णुं शशिवर्णं चतुर्भुजम् । | प्रसन्नवदनं ध्यायेत् सर्वविघ्नोपशान्तये ॥१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śuklāmbaradharaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaśivarṇaṃ caturbhujam,
prasannavadanaṃ dhyāyet sarvavighnōpaśāntaye. (1)
shlokas.meaning_english: One should meditate on Viṣṇu, dressed in white robes, moon-coloured, four-armed, with a cheerful face, for the removal of all obstacles.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यस्य द्विरदवक्त्राद्याः पारिषद्याः परः शतम् ।
विघ्नं निघ्नन्ति सततं विष्वक्सेनं तमाश्रये ॥२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: यस्य द्विरदवक्त्राद्याः पारिषद्याः परः शतम् । | विघ्नं निघ्नन्ति सततं विष्वक्सेनं तमाश्रये ॥२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yasya dviradavaktrādyāḥ pāriṣadyāḥ paraḥ śatam,
vighnaṃ nighnanti satataṃ viṣvakṣenaṃ tam āśraye. (2)
shlokas.meaning_english: I take refuge in Viṣvaksena – whose attendants, led by the elephant- faced one and numbering in the hundreds, ever remove all obstacles.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
व्यासं वसिष्ठनप्तारं शक्तेः पौत्रमकल्मषम् ।
पराशरात्मजं वन्दे शुकतातं तपोनिधिम् ॥३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: व्यासं वसिष्ठनप्तारं शक्तेः पौत्रमकल्मषम् । | पराशरात्मजं वन्दे शुकतातं तपोनिधिम् ॥३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vyāsaṃ vasiṣṭhanaptāraṃ śakteḥ pautramakalmaṣam,
parāśarātmajaṃ vande śukatātaṃ taponidhim. (3)
shlokas.meaning_english: I salute Vyāsa – the great-grandson of Vasiṣṭha, the grandson of Śakti, the immaculate son of Parāśara, the father of Śuka, the treasure of austerities.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
व्यासाय विष्णुरूपाय व्यासरूपाय विष्णवे ।
नमो वै ब्रह्मनिधये वासिष्ठाय नमो नमः ॥४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: व्यासाय विष्णुरूपाय व्यासरूपाय विष्णवे । | नमो वै ब्रह्मनिधये वासिष्ठाय नमो नमः ॥४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vyāsāya viṣṇurūpāya vyāsarūpāya viṣṇave,
namo vai brahmanidhaye vāsiṣṭhāya namo namaḥ. (4)
shlokas.meaning_english: O Vyāsa in the form of Viṣṇu, O Viṣṇu in the form of Vyāsa, O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, O treasure of Brahman – I offer obeisances unto Thee again and again.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अविकाराय शुद्धााय नित्याय परमात्मने ।
सदैकरूपरूपाय विष्णवे सर्वजिष्णवे ॥५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अविकाराय शुद्धााय नित्याय परमात्मने । | सदैकरूपरूपाय विष्णवे सर्वजिष्णवे ॥५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
avikārāya śuddhāya nityāya paramātmane,
sadaikarūparūpāya viṣṇave sarvajiṣṇave. (5)
shlokas.meaning_english: I bow before Viṣṇu – the pure, the unchanging, the eternal, the Supreme Self, ever of one form, ever victorious over all.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यस्य स्मरणमात्रेण जन्मसंसारबन्धनात् ।
विमुच्यते नमस्तस्मै विष्णवे प्रभविष्णवे ॥६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: यस्य स्मरणमात्रेण जन्मसंसारबन्धनात् । | विमुच्यते नमस्तस्मै विष्णवे प्रभविष्णवे ॥६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yasya smaraṇamātreṇa janmasaṃsārabandhanāt,
vimucyate namas tasmai viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave. (6)
shlokas.meaning_english: Obeisance to that Viṣṇu, the all-powerful – whose mere remembrance frees one from the bondage of birth and the cycle of worldly existence.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
श्रीवैशम्पायन उवाच –
श्रुत्वा धर्मानशेषेण पावनानि च सर्वशः ।
युधिष्ठिरः शान्तनवं पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत ॥७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: श्रीवैशम्पायन उवाच – | श्रुत्वा धर्मानशेषेण पावनानि च सर्वशः । | युधिष्ठिरः शान्तनवं पुनरेवाभ्यभाषत ॥७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śrī vaiśampāyana uvāca –
śrutvā dharmānaśeṣeṇa pāvanāni ca sarvaśaḥ,
yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śāntanavaṃ punarevābhyabhāṣata. (7)
shlokas.meaning_english: Śrī Vaiśampāyana said – Having heard the Dharma in its entirety and all the purifying teachings, Yudhiṣṭhira again addressed the son of Śāntanu (Bhīṣma).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच –
किमेकं दैवतं लोके किं वाप्येकं परायणम् ।
स्तुवन्तः कं कमर्चन्तः प्राप्नुयुर्मानवाः शुभम् ॥८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: युधिष्ठिर उवाच – | किमेकं दैवतं लोके किं वाप्येकं परायणम् । | स्तुवन्तः कं कमर्चन्तः प्राप्नुयुर्मानवाः शुभम् ॥८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śrī yudhiṣṭhira uvāca – kim ekaṃ daivataṃ loke kiṃ vāpy ekaṃ
parāyaṇam,
stuvantaḥ kaṃ kam arcantaḥ prāpnuyur mānavāḥ śubham. (8)
shlokas.meaning_english: Yudhiṣṭhira asked – Who is the one God in this world? Who is the one supreme refuge? By praising and worshipping whom do human beings attain good?

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
को धर्मः सर्वधर्माणां भवतः परमो मतः ।
किं जपन्मुच्यते जन्तुर्जन्मसंसारबन्धनात् ॥९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: को धर्मः सर्वधर्माणां भवतः परमो मतः । | किं जपन्मुच्यते जन्तुर्जन्मसंसारबन्धनात् ॥९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ko dharmaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ bhavataḥ paramo mataḥ,
kiṃ japan mucyate jantur janmasaṃsārabandhanāt. (9)
shlokas.meaning_english: Which Dharma do you consider to be the supreme of all Dharmas? By chanting what is a creature freed from the bondage of birth and the cycle of worldly existence?

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच –
जगत्प्रभुं देवदेवमनन्तं पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
स्तुवन्नामसहस्रेण पुरुषः सततोत्थितः ॥१०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भीष्म उवाच – | जगत्प्रभुं देवदेवमनन्तं पुरुषोत्तमम् । | स्तुवन्नामसहस्रेण पुरुषः सततोत्थितः ॥१०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śrī bhīṣma uvāca – jagatprabhuṃ devadevamanantaṃ
puruṣottamam,
stuvan nāmasahasreṇa puruṣaḥ satatotthitaḥ. (10)
shlokas.meaning_english: Bhīṣma replied – Praising the Lord of the universe, the God of gods, the infinite Puruṣottama, with a thousand names, a person ever rises to greatness.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
तमेव चार्चयन्नित्यं भक्त्या पुरुषमव्ययम् ।
ध्यायन् स्तुवन्नमस्यंश्च यजमानस्तमेव च ॥ ११॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: तमेव चार्चयन्नित्यं भक्त्या पुरुषमव्ययम् । | ध्यायन् स्तुवन्नमस्यंश्च यजमानस्तमेव च ॥ ११॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
tam eva cārcayan nityaṃ bhaktyā puruṣam avyayam,
dhyāyan stuvan namasyaṃś ca yajamānas tam eva ca. (11)
shlokas.meaning_english: Worshipping Him alone daily with devotion, meditating on, praising, and bowing to the inexhaustible Puruṣa, and sacrificing to Him alone – [such a person, as said in v.10, ever rises].

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अनादिनिधनं विष्णुं सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् ।
लोकाध्यक्षं स्तुवन्नित्यं सर्वदुःखातिगो भवेत् ॥१२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अनादिनिधनं विष्णुं सर्वलोकमहेश्वरम् । | लोकाध्यक्षं स्तुवन्नित्यं सर्वदुःखातिगो भवेत् ॥१२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
anādinidhanaṃ viṣṇuṃ sarvalokamaheśvaram,
lokādhyakṣaṃ stuvan nityaṃ sarvaduḥkhātigo bhavet. (12)
shlokas.meaning_english: By praising Viṣṇu – who is without beginning or end, the great Lord of all the worlds, the presiding deity of the worlds – one passes beyond all sorrows.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मण्यं सर्वधर्मज्ञं लोकानां कीर्तिवर्धनम् ।
लोकनाथं महद्भूतं सर्वभूतभवोद्भवम् ॥१३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ब्रह्मण्यं सर्वधर्मज्ञं लोकानां कीर्तिवर्धनम् । | लोकनाथं महद्भूतं सर्वभूतभवोद्भवम् ॥१३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
brahmaṇyaṃ sarvadharmajñaṃ lokānāṃ kīrtivardhanam,
lokanāthaṃ mahadbhūtaṃ sarvabhūtabhavodbhavam. (13)
shlokas.meaning_english: He is the support of Brahman, the knower of all dharmas, the enhancer of the glory of the worlds, the Lord of the worlds, the great Being, the source of origin of all beings.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
एष मे सर्वधर्माणां धर्मोऽधिकतमो मतः ।
यद्भक्त्या पुण्डरीकाक्षं स्तवैरर्चेन्नरः सदा ॥१४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: एष मे सर्वधर्माणां धर्मोऽधिकतमो मतः । | यद्भक्त्या पुण्डरीकाक्षं स्तवैरर्चेन्नरः सदा ॥१४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
eṣa me sarvadharmāṇāṃ dharmo dhikatamo mataḥ,
yad bhaktyā puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ stavair arcen naraḥ sadā. (14)
shlokas.meaning_english: This is the Dharma I consider highest of all – that one should always worship the lotus-eyed Lord with devotion and hymns.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
परमं यो महत्तेजः परमं यो महत्तपः ।
परमं यो महद्ब्रह्म परमं यः परायणम् ॥१५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: परमं यो महत्तेजः परमं यो महत्तपः । | परमं यो महद्ब्रह्म परमं यः परायणम् ॥१५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
paramaṃ yo mahattejāḥ paramaṃ yo mahattapaḥ,
paramaṃ yo mahadbrahma paramaṃ yaḥ parāyaṇam. (15)
shlokas.meaning_english: He is the supreme great light; He is the supreme great austerity; He is the supreme great Brahman (Absolute); He is the supreme highest goal.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
पवित्राणां पवित्रं यो मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ।
दैवतं दैवतानां च भूतानां योऽव्ययः पिता ॥१६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: पवित्राणां पवित्रं यो मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् । | दैवतं दैवतानां च भूतानां योऽव्ययः पिता ॥१६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ yo maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam,
daivataṃ daivatānāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ yo 'vyayaḥ pitā. (16)
shlokas.meaning_english: He who is the most holy among the holy and the most auspicious among the auspicious, who is the God of gods and the inexhaustible Father of all beings.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यतः सर्वाणि भूतानि भवन्त्यादियुगागमे ।
यस्मिंश्च प्रलयं यान्ति पुनरेव युगक्षये ॥१७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: यतः सर्वाणि भूतानि भवन्त्यादियुगागमे । | यस्मिंश्च प्रलयं यान्ति पुनरेव युगक्षये ॥१७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yataḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhavanty ādiyugāgame,
yasmiṃś ca pralayaṃ yānti punar eva yugakṣaye. (17)
shlokas.meaning_english: From Him all creatures proceed at the beginning of an age, and in Him they are absorbed again at the end of the age.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
तस्य लोकप्रधानस्य जगन्नाथस्य भूपते ।
विष्णोर्नामसहस्रं मे श्रृणु पापभयापहम् ॥१८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: तस्य लोकप्रधानस्य जगन्नाथस्य भूपते । | विष्णोर्नामसहस्रं मे श्रृणु पापभयापहम् ॥१८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
tasya lokapradhānasya jagannāthasya bhūpate,
viṣṇor nāmasahasraṃ me śṛṇu pāpabhayāpaham. (18)
shlokas.meaning_english: Of that Chief of the world, of the Lord of the universe, O King – hear from me the thousand names of Viṣṇu, which remove all sin and fear.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यानि नामानि गौणानि विख्यातानि महात्मनः ।
ऋषिभिः परिगीतानि तानि वक्ष्यामि भूतये ॥१९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: यानि नामानि गौणानि विख्यातानि महात्मनः । | ऋषिभिः परिगीतानि तानि वक्ष्यामि भूतये ॥१९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yāni nāmāni gauṇāni vikhyātāni mahātmanaḥ,
ṛṣibhiḥ parigītāni tāni vakṣyāmi bhūtaye. (19)
shlokas.meaning_english: Those famous names of the Great Soul which reveal His manifold qualities, celebrated by rishis (seers), I shall declare for the good of all.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ऋषिर्नाम्नां सहस्रस्य वेदव्यासो महामुनिः ।
छन्दोऽनुष्टुप् तथा देवो भगवान् देवकीसुतः ॥२०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ऋषिर्नाम्नां सहस्रस्य वेदव्यासो महामुनिः । | छन्दोऽनुष्टुप् तथा देवो भगवान् देवकीसुतः ॥२०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ṛṣirnāmnāṃ sahasrasya vedavyāsō mahāmuniḥ,
chandōnuṣṭup tathā devō bhagavān devakīsutaḥ. (20)
shlokas.meaning_english: The rishi of the thousand names is Vedavyāsa, the great contemplative sage. The metre is Anuṣṭup, and the deity is the blessed son of Devakī (Kṛṣṇa).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अमृतांशूद्भवो बीजं शक्तिर्देवकिनन्दनः ।
त्रिसामा हृदयं तस्य शान्त्यर्थे विनियुज्यते ॥२१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अमृतांशूद्भवो बीजं शक्तिर्देवकिनन्दनः । | त्रिसामा हृदयं तस्य शान्त्यर्थे विनियुज्यते ॥२१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bījaṃ śaktir devakinandanaḥ,
trisāmā hṛdayaṃ tasya śāntyarthe viniyujyate. (21)
shlokas.meaning_english: The bīja (seed-syllable) is He born of the nectar-rayed one (Moon); the śakti (power) is the son of Devakī; Trisāmā is assigned to the heart; the purpose is the attainment of peace.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
विष्णुं जिष्णुं महाविष्णुं प्रभविष्णुं महेश्वरम् ।
अनेकरूप दैत्यान्तं नमामि पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥२२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: विष्णुं जिष्णुं महाविष्णुं प्रभविष्णुं महेश्वरम् । | अनेकरूप दैत्यान्तं नमामि पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥२२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
viṣṇuṃ jiṣṇuṃ mahāviṣṇuṃ prabhaviṣṇuṃ maheśvaram,
anekarūpa daityāntaṃ namāmi puruṣottamam. (22)
shlokas.meaning_english: I bow to Viṣṇu, the Conqueror, the Great Viṣṇu, the Creator, the Great Lord – He of many forms, the Destroyer of demons, the Supreme Person.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ॐ अस्य श्रीविष्णोर्दिव्यसहस्रनामस्तोत्रमहामन्त्रस्य ।
श्रीवेदव्यासो भगवान् ऋषिः ।
अनुष्टुप् छन्दः ।
श्रीमहाविष्णुः परमात्मा श्रीमन्नारायणो देवता ।
अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुरिति बीजम् ।
देवकीनन्दनः स्रष्टेति शक्तिः ।
उद्भवः क्षोभणो देव इति परमो मन्त्रः ।
शङ्खभृन्नन्दकी चक्रीति कीलकम् ।
शार्ङ्गधन्वा गदाधर इत्यस्त्रम् ।
रथाङ्गपाणिरक्षोभ्य इति नेत्रम् ।
त्रिसामा सामगः सामेति कवचम् ।
आनन्दं परब्रह्मेति योनिः ।
ऋतुः सुदर्शनः काल इति दिग्बन्धः ।
श्रीविश्वरूप इति ध्यानम् ।
श्रीमहाविष्णुप्रीत्यर्थे सहस्रनामपारायणे विनियोगः ॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ॐ अस्य श्रीविष्णोर्दिव्यसहस्रनामस्तोत्रमहामन्त्रस्य । | श्रीवेदव्यासो भगवान् ऋषिः । | अनुष्टुप् छन्दः । | श्रीमहाविष्णुः परमात्मा श्रीमन्नारायणो देवता । | अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुरिति बीजम् । | देवकीनन्दनः स्रष्टेति शक्तिः । | उद्भवः क्षोभणो देव इति परमो मन्त्रः । | शङ्खभृन्नन्दकी चक्रीति कीलकम् । | शार्ङ्गधन्वा गदाधर इत्यस्त्रम् । | रथाङ्गपाणिरक्षोभ्य इति नेत्रम् । | त्रिसामा सामगः सामेति कवचम् । | आनन्दं परब्रह्मेति योनिः । | ऋतुः सुदर्शनः काल इति दिग्बन्धः । | श्रीविश्वरूप इति ध्यानम् । | श्रीमहाविष्णुप्रीत्यर्थे सहस्रनामपारायणे विनियोगः ॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
oṃ asya śrīviṣṇordivyasahasranāmastotramahāmantrasya,
śrīvedavyāso bhagavān ṛṣiḥ,
anuṣṭup chandaḥ,
śrīmahāviṣṇuḥ paramātmā śrīmannārāyaṇo devatā,
amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bhānuriti bījam,
devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭeti śaktiḥ,
udbhavaḥ kṣobhaṇo deva iti paramo mantraḥ,
śaṅkhabhṛnnandakī cakrīti kīlakam,
śārṅgadhanvā gadādhara ityastram,
rathāṅgapāṇirakṣobhya iti netram,
trisāmā sāmagaḥ sāmeti kavacam,
ānandaṃ parabrahmeti yoniḥ,
ṛtuḥ sudarśanaḥ kāla iti digbandhaḥ,
śrīviśvarūpa iti dhyānam,
śrīmahāviṣṇuprītyarthe sahasranāmapārāyaṇe viniyogaḥ.
Of this great mantra-hymn of the divine thousand names of Śrī Viṣṇu –
the venerable Vedavyāsa is the seer (ṛṣi); the metre is Anuṣṭup; Śrī
Mahāviṣṇu, the Supreme Self, Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, is the deity (devatā);
Amṛtāṃśūdbhava Bhānu ("the Sun, born of the nectar-rayed one") is
the seed (bīja); Devakīnandanaḥ Sraṣṭā ("the son of Devakī, the
Creator") is the power (śakti); Udbhava, Kṣobhaṇa, Deva is the supreme
mantra; Śaṅkhabhṛt, Nandakī, Cakrī ("Bearer of the conch, Wielder of
Nandaka, Bearer of the discus") is the pin (kīlaka); Śārṅgadhanvā,
Gadādhara ("He of the Śārṅga bow, the Mace-bearer") is the weapon
(astra); Rathāṅgapāṇi, Akṣobhya ("He who holds the wheel, the
Imperturbable") is the eye (netra); Trisāmā, Sāmagaḥ, Sāma is the
armour (kavaca); Ānanda, Parabrahma is the womb/source (yoni); Ṛtu,
Sudarśana, Kāla is the directional binding (digbandha); Śrī Viśvarūpa is
the meditation (dhyāna). This recitation of the thousand names is
undertaken for the gratification of Śrī Mahāviṣṇu (viniyoga).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
क्षीरोदन्वत्प्रदेशे शुचिमणिविलसत्सैकते मौक्तिकानां
मालाक्लृप्तासनस्थः स्फटिकमणिनिभैर्मौक्तिकैर्मण्डिताङ्गः ।
शुभ्रैरभ्रैरदभ्रैरुपरिविरचितैर्मुक्तपीयूषवर्षैः
आनन्दी नः पुनीयादरिनलिनगदाशङ्खपाणिर्मुकुन्दः ॥१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: क्षीरोदन्वत्प्रदेशे शुचिमणिविलसत्सैकते मौक्तिकानां | मालाक्लृप्तासनस्थः स्फटिकमणिनिभैर्मौक्तिकैर्मण्डिताङ्गः । | शुभ्रैरभ्रैरदभ्रैरुपरिविरचितैर्मुक्तपीयूषवर्षैः | आनन्दी नः पुनीयादरिनलिनगदाशङ्खपाणिर्मुकुन्दः ॥१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
kṣīrodanvatpradeśe śucimaṇivilasatsaikate mauktikānāṃ
mālākḷptāsanasthaḥ sphaṭikamaṇinibhair mauktikair maṇḍitāṅgaḥ,
śubhrair abhrair adabhrair upariviracitair muktapīyūṣavarṣaiḥ
ānandī naḥ punīyād arinalinaagadāśaṅkhapāṇir mukundaḥ. (1)
shlokas.meaning_english: In the region of the milk-ocean, seated upon a throne fashioned from a garland of pure gems and pearls, His body adorned with crystal-like pearls, amidst white and abundant clouds raining pure nectar from above – may Mukunda, the destroyer of foes, bearing lotus, mace and conch in his hands, fill us with bliss and purify us.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भूः पादौ यस्य नाभिर्वियदसुरनिलश्चन्द्र सूर्यौ च नेत्रे
कर्णावाशाः शिरो द्यौौर्मुखमपि दहनो यस्य वासो यमब्धिः ।
अन्तःस्थं यस्य विश्वं सुरनरखगगोभोगिगन्धर्वदैत्यैः
चित्रं रं रम्यते तं त्रिभुवन वपुषं विष्णुमीशं नमामि ॥२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भूः पादौ यस्य नाभिर्वियदसुरनिलश्चन्द्र सूर्यौ च नेत्रे | कर्णावाशाः शिरो द्यौौर्मुखमपि दहनो यस्य वासो यमब्धिः । | अन्तःस्थं यस्य विश्वं सुरनरखगगोभोगिगन्धर्वदैत्यैः | चित्रं रं रम्यते तं त्रिभुवन वपुषं विष्णुमीशं नमामि ॥२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
bhūḥ pādau yasya nābhir viyad asuranilaś candra sūryau ca netre
karṇāv āśāḥ śiro dyaur mukham api dahano yasya vāso 'mabdhiḥ,
antaḥsthaṃ yasya viśvaṃ suranara khagago bhogi gandharva
daityaiḥ,
citraṃ raṃ ramyate taṃ tribhuvana vapuṣaṃ viṣṇum īśaṃ namāmi.
(2)
shlokas.meaning_english: I bow before Viṣṇu, the Lord of three worlds – whose feet are the earth, whose navel is the sky, whose vital breath is the air, whose eyes are the moon and sun, whose ears are the four directions, whose head is the realm of gods, whose mouth is fire, whose garment is the ocean – and within whose belly play and rejoice the gods, men, birds, animals, serpent-beings, Gandharvas and Asuras.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ॐ शान्ताकारं भुजगशयनं पद्मनाभं सुरेशं
विश्वााधारं गगनसदृशं मेघवर्णं शुभाङ्गम् ।
लक्ष्मीकान्तं कमलनयनं योगिभिर्ध्यानगम्यं
वन्दे विष्णुं भवभयहरं सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ॐ शान्ताकारं भुजगशयनं पद्मनाभं सुरेशं | विश्वााधारं गगनसदृशं मेघवर्णं शुभाङ्गम् । | लक्ष्मीकान्तं कमलनयनं योगिभिर्ध्यानगम्यं | वन्दे विष्णुं भवभयहरं सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
oṃ śāntākāraṃ bhujagaśayanaṃ padmanābhaṃ sureśaṃ
viśvādhāraṃ gaganasadṛśaṃ meghavarṇaṃ śubhāṅgam,
lakṣmīkāntaṃ kamalanayanaṃ yogibhir dhyānagamyaṃ
vande viṣṇuṃ bhavabhayaharaṃ sarvalokaikanātham. (3)
shlokas.meaning_english: I bow before Viṣṇu – the personification of peace, who sleeps on the coils of the serpent, who has a lotus in his navel, the Lord of gods, the support of the universe, vast as the sky, dark as a raincloud, with beautiful limbs, the beloved of Lakṣmī, with lotus-like eyes, attainable by yogis through meditation, the destroyer of the fear of worldly existence, the sole Lord of all worlds.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
मेघश्यामं पीतकौशेयवासं
श्रीवत्साङ्कं कौस्तुभोद्भाासिताङ्गम् ।
पुण्योपेतं पुण्डरीकायताक्षं
विष्णुं वन्दे सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: मेघश्यामं पीतकौशेयवासं | श्रीवत्साङ्कं कौस्तुभोद्भाासिताङ्गम् । | पुण्योपेतं पुण्डरीकायताक्षं | विष्णुं वन्दे सर्वलोकैकनाथम् ॥४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
meghaśyāmaṃ pītakauśeyavāsaṃ
śrīvatsāṅkaṃ kaustubhodbhāsitāṅgam,
puṇyopetaṃ puṇḍarīkāyatākṣaṃ
viṣṇuṃ vande sarvalokaikanātham. (4)
shlokas.meaning_english: I bow before Viṣṇu, the sole Lord of all the universe – dark as a raincloud, wearing yellow silk, bearing the Śrīvatsa mark, with limbs radiant from the Kaustubha gem, endowed with all auspiciousness, with eyes expansive as a full-blown lotus.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
नमः समस्तभूतानामादिभूताय भूभृते ।
अनेकरूपरूपाय विष्णवे प्रभविष्णवे ॥५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: नमः समस्तभूतानामादिभूताय भूभृते । | अनेकरूपरूपाय विष्णवे प्रभविष्णवे ॥५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
namaḥ samastabhūtānām ādibhūtāya bhūbhṛte,
anekarūparūpāya viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave. (5)
shlokas.meaning_english: Obeisance to Viṣṇu – the primordial source of all beings, the sustainer of the earth, He of manifold forms, the all-powerful originator.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सशङ्खचक्रंं सकिरीटकुण्डलं
सपीतवस्त्रं सरसीरुहेक्षणम् ।
सहारवक्षःस्थलशोभिकौस्तुभं
नमामि विष्णुं शिरसा चतुर्भुजम् ॥६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सशङ्खचक्रंं सकिरीटकुण्डलं | सपीतवस्त्रं सरसीरुहेक्षणम् । | सहारवक्षःस्थलशोभिकौस्तुभं | नमामि विष्णुं शिरसा चतुर्भुजम् ॥६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
saśaṅkhacakraṃ sakirīṭakuṇḍalaṃ
sapītavastraṃ sarasīruhekṣaṇam,
sahāravakṣaḥsthalaśobhikaustubhaṃ
namāmi viṣṇuṃ śirasā caturbhujam. (6)
shlokas.meaning_english: I bow my head before Viṣṇu – four-armed, bearing conch and discus, wearing crown and earrings, clad in yellow silk, with lotus-like eyes, the Kaustubha gem glowing on his garlanded chest.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
छायायां पारिजातस्य हेमसिंहासनोपरि
आसीनमम्बुदश्यामामायताक्षमलंकृतम् ।
चन्द्राननं चतुर्बाहुं श्रीवत्साङ्कित वक्षसम्
रुक्मिणीसत्यभामाभ्यां सहितं कृष्णमाश्रये ॥७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: छायायां पारिजातस्य हेमसिंहासनोपरि | आसीनमम्बुदश्यामामायताक्षमलंकृतम् । | चन्द्राननं चतुर्बाहुं श्रीवत्साङ्कित वक्षसम् | रुक्मिणीसत्यभामाभ्यां सहितं कृष्णमाश्रये ॥७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
chāyāyāṃ pārijātasya hemasiṃhāsanopari
āsīnam ambudaśyāmam āyatākṣam alaṃkṛtam,
candrānanaṃ caturbāhuṃ śrīvatsāṅkita vakṣasam
rukmiṇīsatyabhāmābhyāṃ sahitaṃ kṛṣṇam āśraye. (7)
shlokas.meaning_english: I seek refuge in Lord Kṛṣṇa – seated on a golden throne in the shade of the Pārijāta tree, dark as a raincloud, with wide eyes, beautifully adorned, with a moon-like face, four arms, and a chest bearing the Śrīvatsa mark – in the company of Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कारो भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः ।
भूतकृद् भूतभृद्भावो भूतात्मा भूतभावनः ॥१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: विश्वं विष्णुर्वषट्कारो भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः । | भूतकृद् भूतभृद्भावो भूतात्मा भूतभावनः ॥१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
viśvaṃ viṣṇur vaṣaṭkāro bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ,
bhūtakṛd bhūtabhṛd bhāvo bhūtātmā bhūtabhāvanaḥ. (1)
shlokas.meaning_english: Viśvaṃ: The all or the Universe.; Viṣṇuḥ: He who pervades everything.; Vaṣaṭkāraḥ: He for whom the sacrificial verses are uttered in yajñas.; Bhūta: bhavya-bhavat-prabhuḥ – The master who transcends past, present and future.; Bhūtakṛd: The creator and destroyer of all existences in the universe.; Bhūtabhṛd: One who supports, sustains and governs the universe.; Bhāvaḥ: Pure existence.; Bhūtātmā: The essence of all beings.; Bhūta: bhāvanaḥ – He who originates and develops all elements.

padas.meaning: The all or the Universe.
He who pervades everything.
He for whom the sacrificial verses are uttered in yajñas.
bhavya-bhavat-prabhuḥ – The master who transcends past, present and future.
The creator and destroyer of all existences in the universe.
One who supports, sustains and governs the universe.
Pure existence.
The essence of all beings.
bhāvanaḥ – He who originates and develops all elements.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः ।
अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञोऽक्षर एव च ॥२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: पूतात्मा परमात्मा च मुक्तानां परमा गतिः । | अव्ययः पुरुषः साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञोऽक्षर एव च ॥२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
pūtātmā paramātmā ca muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ,
avyayaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣī kṣetrajño 'kṣara eva ca. (2)
shlokas.meaning_english: Pūtātmā: One whose nature is purity.; Paramātmā: The supreme Self.; Muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ: The highest goal of the liberated ones.; Avyayaḥ: One for whom there is no decay.; Puruṣaḥ: One who abides in the body (pura).; Sākṣī: One who witnesses everything.; Kṣetrajñaḥ: The knower of the field (body).; Akṣaraḥ: He who is indestructible.

padas.meaning: One whose nature is purity.
The supreme Self.
The highest goal of the liberated ones.
One for whom there is no decay.
One who abides in the body (pura).
One who witnesses everything.
The knower of the field (body).
He who is indestructible.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
योगो योगविदां नेता प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः ।
नारसिंहवपुः श्रीमान् केशवः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: योगो योगविदां नेता प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः । | नारसिंहवपुः श्रीमान् केशवः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yogo yogavidāṃ netā pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ,
nārasiṃhavapuḥ śrīmān keśavaḥ puruṣottamaḥ. (3)
shlokas.meaning_english: Yogaḥ: One attainable through Yoga.; Yogavidāṃ netā: The master of those established in Yoga.; Pradhāna: puruṣeśvaraḥ – The master of Pradhāna (Prakṛti) and Puruṣa (Jīva).; Nārasiṃha: vapuḥ – One who combined the bodies of a man and a lion.; Śrīmān: One on whose chest the goddess Śrī always dwells.; Keśavaḥ: One whose locks (keśa) are beautiful.; Puruṣottamaḥ: The greatest among all Puruṣas.

padas.meaning: One attainable through Yoga.
The master of those established in Yoga.
puruṣeśvaraḥ – The master of Pradhāna (Prakṛti) and Puruṣa (Jīva).
vapuḥ – One who combined the bodies of a man and a lion.
One on whose chest the goddess Śrī always dwells.
One whose locks (keśa) are beautiful.
The greatest among all Puruṣas.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सर्वः शर्वः शिवः स्थाणुर्भूतादिर्निधिरव्ययः ।
सम्भवो भावनो भर्ता प्रभवः प्रभुरीश्वरः ॥४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सर्वः शर्वः शिवः स्थाणुर्भूतादिर्निधिरव्ययः । | सम्भवो भावनो भर्ता प्रभवः प्रभुरीश्वरः ॥४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sarvaḥ śarvaḥ śivaḥ sthāṇur bhūtādir nidhir avyayaḥ,
saṃbhavo bhāvano bhartā prabhavaḥ prabhur īśvaraḥ. (4)

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
स्वयम्भूः शम्भुरादित्यः पुष्कराक्षो महास्वनः ।
अनादिनिधनो धाता विधाता धातुरुत्तमः ॥५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: स्वयम्भूः शम्भुरादित्यः पुष्कराक्षो महास्वनः । | अनादिनिधनो धाता विधाता धातुरुत्तमः ॥५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
svayaṃbhūḥ śambhur ādityaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāsvanaḥ,
anādinidhano dhātā vidhātā dhāturuttamaḥ. (5)
shlokas.meaning_english: Svayambhūḥ: One who exists by Himself, uncaused.; Śambhuḥ: One who bestows happiness on devotees.; Ādityaḥ: The golden-hued person in the sun's orb.; Puṣkarākṣaḥ: One with eyes resembling lotus petals.; Mahāsvanaḥ: One from whom comes the great sound – the Veda.; Anādi: nidhanaḥ – The one existence that has neither beginning nor end.; Dhātā: One who is the support of the universe.; Vidhātā: He who generates Karmas and their fruits.; Dhāturuttamaḥ: The ultimate support of everything.

One who bestows happiness on devotees.
The golden-hued person in the sun's orb.
One with eyes resembling lotus petals.

nidhanaḥ – The one existence that has neither beginning nor end.
One who is the support of the universe.
He who generates Karmas and their fruits.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अप्रमेयो हृषीकेशः पद्मनाभोऽमरप्रभुः ।
विश्वकर्मा मनुस्त्वष्टा स्थविष्ठः स्थविरो ध्रुवः ॥६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अप्रमेयो हृषीकेशः पद्मनाभोऽमरप्रभुः । | विश्वकर्मा मनुस्त्वष्टा स्थविष्ठः स्थविरो ध्रुवः ॥६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
aprameyo hṛṣīkeśaḥ padmanābho 'maraprabhuḥ,
viśvakarmā manus tvaṣṭā sthaviṣṭhaḥ sthaviro dhruvaḥ. (6)
shlokas.meaning_english: Aprameyaḥ: One not measurable by any means of knowledge.; Hṛṣīkeśaḥ: The master of the senses.; Padmanābhaḥ: He in whose navel stands the lotus, the source of the universe.; Amara: prabhuḥ – The master of the immortal ones (Devas).; Viśvakarmā: He whose works have resulted in all that exists.; Manuḥ: He who thinks.; Tvaṣṭā: He who makes all beings contract at the time of cosmic dissolution.; Sthaviṣṭhaḥ: He who excels in bulk and substantiality.; Sthaviraḥ: dhruvaḥ – The eternal, most ancient and unchanging One.

The master of the senses.

prabhuḥ – The master of the immortal ones (Devas).

He who thinks.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अग्राह्यः शाश्वतः कृष्णो लोहिताक्षः प्रतर्दनः ।
प्रभूतस्त्रिककुब्धाम पवित्रं मङ्गलं परम् ॥७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अग्राह्यः शाश्वतः कृष्णो लोहिताक्षः प्रतर्दनः । | प्रभूतस्त्रिककुब्धाम पवित्रं मङ्गलं परम् ॥७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
agrāhyaḥ śāśvataḥ kṛṣṇo lohitākṣaḥ pratardanaḥ,
prabhūtas trikakubdhāma pavitraṃ maṅgalaṃ param. (7)
shlokas.meaning_english: Agrāhyaḥ: One who cannot be grasped by the organs of knowledge.; Śāśvataḥ: One who exists at all times.; Kṛṣṇaḥ: Existence-Knowledge-Bliss.; Lohitākṣaḥ: One whose eyes are tinged red.; Pratardanaḥ: Destroyer of all at the time of cosmic dissolution.; Prabhūtaḥ: Great because of unique qualities like omnipotence and omniscience.; Tri: kakub-dhāma – The support of the three regions – above, below and in the middle.; Pavitraṃ: That which purifies everything; Maṅgalaṃ param: Supremely auspicious.

Existence-Knowledge-Bliss.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः ।
हिरण्यगर्भो भूगर्भो माधवो मधुसूदनः ॥८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ईशानः प्राणदः प्राणो ज्येष्ठः श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः । | हिरण्यगर्भो भूगर्भो माधवो मधुसूदनः ॥८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
īśānaḥ prāṇadaḥ prāṇo jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ,
hiraṇyagarbho bhūgarbho mādhavo madhusūdanaḥ. (8)
shlokas.meaning_english: Īśānaḥ: He who controls and regulates everything.; Prāṇadaḥ: One who bestows and activates Prāṇa, the vital energy; Prāṇaḥ: The Supreme Being.; Jyeṣṭhaḥ: The eldest of all; for there is nothing before Him.; Śreṣṭhaḥ: One deserving the highest praise.; Prajāpatiḥ: The master of all living beings.; Hiraṇyagarbhaḥ: One who is the Ātman of even Brahmā the creator.; Bhūgarbhaḥ: One who has the world within Himself.; Mādhavaḥ: The Consort of Mā (Mahālakṣmī); or one known through Madhu-Vidyā.; Madhusūdanaḥ: The destroyer of the demon Madhu.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ईश्वरो विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः ।
अनुत्तमो दुराधर्षः कृतज्ञः कृतिरात्मवान् ॥९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ईश्वरो विक्रमी धन्वी मेधावी विक्रमः क्रमः । | अनुत्तमो दुराधर्षः कृतज्ञः कृतिरात्मवान् ॥९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
īśvaro vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ,
anuttamo durādharṣaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kṛtir ātmavān. (9)
shlokas.meaning_english: Īśvaraḥ: The Omnipotent Being.; Vikramī: The courageous One.; Dhanvī: One armed with a bow.; Medhāvī: He of great intelligence capable of grasping all texts.; Vikramaḥ: He who transcends saṃsāra; or one whose mount is Garuḍa.; Kramaḥ: The cause of crossing the ocean of saṃsāra for devotees.; Anuttamaḥ: He than whom there is none greater.; Durādharṣaḥ: One whom none can overcome.; Kṛtajñaḥ: One who knows everything done by Jīvas; pleased even by simple offerings.; Kṛtiḥ: That which is achieved through all human effort.; Ātmavān: One established in His own greatness, requiring no other support.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सुरेशः शरणं शर्म विश्वरेताः प्रजाभवः ।
अहः संवत्सरो व्यालः प्रत्ययः सर्वदर्शनः ॥१०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सुरेशः शरणं शर्म विश्वरेताः प्रजाभवः । | अहः संवत्सरो व्यालः प्रत्ययः सर्वदर्शनः ॥१०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sureśaḥ śaraṇaṃ śarma viśvaretāḥ prajābhavaḥ,

shlokas.meaning_english: Sureśaḥ: The lord of the Suras (Devas).; Śaraṇaṃ: One who removes the sorrows of those in distress.; Śarma: One who is of the nature of supreme bliss.; Viśvaretāḥ: The seed of the universe.; Prajābhavaḥ: He from whom all beings have originated.; Ahaḥ: The luminous one.; Saṃvatsaraḥ: As Time is a form of Viṣṇu, He is called Saṃvatsara (a year).; Vyālaḥ: Being ungraspable like a serpent.; Pratyayaḥ: One of the nature of Prajñā (consciousness).; Sarva: darśanaḥ – One with eyes everywhere.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अजः सर्वेश्वरः सिद्धः सिद्धिः सर्वादिरच्युतः ।

shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ajaḥ sarveśvaraḥ siddhaḥ siddhiḥ sarvādy acyutaḥ,

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वसुर्वसुमनाः सत्यः समात्माऽसम्मितः समः ।

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
रुद्रो बहुशिरा बभ्रुर्विश्वयोनिः शुचिश्रवाः ।

सर्वगः सर्वविद्भानुर्विष्वक्सेनो जनार्दनः ।

shlokas.full_sanskrit:

भ्रााजिष्णुर्भोजनं भोक्ता सहिष्णुर्जगदादिजः ।

उपेन्द्रो वामनः प्रांशुरमोघः शुचिरूर्जितः ।
अतीन्द्रः सङ्ग्रहः सर्गो धृतात्मा नियमो यमः ॥१७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: उपेन्द्रो वामनः प्रांशुरमोघः शुचिरूर्जितः । | अतीन्द्रः सङ्ग्रहः सर्गो धृतात्मा नियमो यमः ॥१७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
upendro vāmanaḥ prāṃśur amoghaḥ śucir ūrjitaḥ,
atīndraḥ saṅgrahaḥ sargo dhṛtātmā niyamo yamaḥ. (17)
shlokas.meaning_english: Upendraḥ: One born as the younger brother of Indra.; Vāmanaḥ: One who in the form of the dwarf went begging to Bali.; Prāṃśuḥ: One of great height.; Amoghaḥ: One whose acts do not go in vain.; Śuciḥ: One who purifies those who adore and praise Him.; Ūrjitaḥ: One of infinite strength.; Atīndraḥ: One who is superior to Indra.; Saṅgrahaḥ: One who is of the subtle form of the universe to be created.; Sargaḥ: The creator of Himself.; Dhṛtātmā: One ever in His inherent form, without transformation.; Niyamaḥ: One who appoints creatures to their particular stations.; Yamaḥ: One who regulates all, remaining within them.

padas.meaning: One born as the younger brother of Indra.
One who in the form of the dwarf went begging to Bali.
One of great height.
One whose acts do not go in vain.
One who purifies those who adore and praise Him.
One of infinite strength.
One who is superior to Indra.
One who is of the subtle form of the universe to be created.
The creator of Himself.
One ever in His inherent form, without transformation.
One who appoints creatures to their particular stations.
One who regulates all, remaining within them.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वेद्योो वैद्यः सदायोगी वीरहा माधवो मधुः ।
अतीन्द्रियो महामायो महोत्साहो महाबलः ॥१८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: वेद्योो वैद्यः सदायोगी वीरहा माधवो मधुः । | अतीन्द्रियो महामायो महोत्साहो महाबलः ॥१८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vedyo vaidyaḥ sadāyogī vīrahā mādhavo madhuḥ,
atīndriyo mahāmāyo mahotsāho mahābalaḥ. (18)
shlokas.meaning_english: Vedyaḥ: One who has to be known by those who aspire for Mokṣa.; Vaidyaḥ: One who knows all branches of knowledge.; Sadāyogī: One who is ever experienceable, being ever existent.; Vīrahā: One who destroys heroic Asuras for the protection of Dharma.; Mādhavaḥ: One who is the Lord or Master of Mā (knowledge).; Madhuḥ: Honey – because the Lord gives joy, just like honey.; Atīndriyaḥ: One who is not knowable by the senses.; Mahāmāyaḥ: One who can cause illusion even over great illusionists.; Mahotsāhaḥ: One ever busy in the work of creation, sustentation and dissolution.; Mahābalaḥ: The strongest among all who have strength.

padas.meaning: One who has to be known by those who aspire for Mokṣa.
One who knows all branches of knowledge.
One who is ever experienceable, being ever existent.
One who destroys heroic Asuras for the protection of Dharma.
One who is the Lord or Master of Mā (knowledge).
Honey – because the Lord gives joy, just like honey.
One who is not knowable by the senses.
One who can cause illusion even over great illusionists.
One ever busy in the work of creation, sustentation and dissolution.
The strongest among all who have strength.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
महाबुद्धिर्महावीर्यो महाशक्तिर्महाद्युतिः ।
अनिर्देश्यवपुः श्रीमानमेयात्मा महाद्रिधृक् ॥१९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: महाबुद्धिर्महावीर्यो महाशक्तिर्महाद्युतिः । | अनिर्देश्यवपुः श्रीमानमेयात्मा महाद्रिधृक् ॥१९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
mahābuddhir mahāvīryo mahāśaktir mahādyutiḥ,
anirdeśyavapuḥ śrīmān ameyātmā mahādridhṛk. (19)
shlokas.meaning_english: Mahābuddhiḥ: The wisest among the wise.; Mahāvīryaḥ: The most powerful one.; Mahāśaktiḥ: One with great resources of strength and skill.; Mahādyutiḥ: One who is intensely brilliant both within and without.; Anirdeśya: vapuḥ – One whose form cannot be indicated as 'He is this'.; Śrīmān: One endowed with greatness of every kind.; Ameyātmā: The Spirit with intelligence that cannot be measured.; Mahādridhṛk: One who held up the great mountain Mandara and also Govardhana.

padas.meaning: The wisest among the wise.
The most powerful one.
One with great resources of strength and skill.
One who is intensely brilliant both within and without.
vapuḥ – One whose form cannot be indicated as 'He is this'.
One endowed with greatness of every kind.
The Spirit with intelligence that cannot be measured.
One who held up the great mountain Mandara and also Govardhana.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
महेष्वासो महीभर्ता श्रीनिवासः सतां गतिः ।
अनिरुद्धः सुरानन्दो गोविन्दो गोविदां पतिः ॥२०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: महेष्वासो महीभर्ता श्रीनिवासः सतां गतिः । | अनिरुद्धः सुरानन्दो गोविन्दो गोविदां पतिः ॥२०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
maheṣvāso mahībhartā śrīnivāsaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ,
aniruddhaḥ surānando govindo govidāṃ patiḥ. (20)
shlokas.meaning_english: Maheṣvāsaḥ: One equipped with the great bow.; Mahībhartā: One who held up the earth submerged in Pralaya waters.; Śrīnivāsaḥ: One on whose chest the Goddess Śrī dwells.; Satāṃgatiḥ: One who bestows the highest destiny to all holy men.; Aniruddhaḥ: One who has never been obstructed in manifesting in various forms.; Surānandaḥ: One who bestows joy on all divinities.; Govindaḥ: Gau means words; He who pervades all words, giving them power.; Govidāṃ patiḥ: The master of all words and their knowers.

padas.meaning: One equipped with the great bow.
One who held up the earth submerged in Pralaya waters.
One on whose chest the Goddess Śrī dwells.
One who bestows the highest destiny to all holy men.
One who has never been obstructed in manifesting in various forms.
One who bestows joy on all divinities.
Gau means words; He who pervades all words, giving them power.
The master of all words and their knowers.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
मरीचिर्दमनो हंसः सुपर्णो भुजगोत्तमः ।
हिरण्यनाभः सुतपाः पद्मनाभः प्रजापतिः ॥२१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: मरीचिर्दमनो हंसः सुपर्णो भुजगोत्तमः । | हिरण्यनाभः सुतपाः पद्मनाभः प्रजापतिः ॥२१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
marīcir damano haṃsaḥ suparṇo bhujagottamaḥ,
hiraṇyanābhaḥ sutapāḥ padmanābhaḥ prajāpatiḥ. (21)
shlokas.meaning_english: Marīciḥ: The supreme power and impressiveness in virtuous persons.; Damanaḥ: One who as Yama inflicts punishments on the unrighteous.; Haṃsaḥ: One who removes the fear of Saṃsāra from those who meditate on Him.; Suparṇaḥ: One who has two wings in the shape of Dharma and Adharma.; Bhujagottamaḥ: One who is the greatest of those who move on arms (serpents).; Hiraṇyanābhaḥ: From whose golden navel arose Brahmā the creator.; Sutapāḥ: One who performs rigorous austerities at Badarikāśrama.; Padmanābhaḥ: One whose navel is beautifully shaped like a lotus.; Prajāpatiḥ: The father of all beings, who are His children.

padas.meaning: The supreme power and impressiveness in virtuous persons.
One who as Yama inflicts punishments on the unrighteous.
One who removes the fear of Saṃsāra from those who meditate on Him.
One who has two wings in the shape of Dharma and Adharma.
One who is the greatest of those who move on arms (serpents).
From whose golden navel arose Brahmā the creator.
One who performs rigorous austerities at Badarikāśrama.
One whose navel is beautifully shaped like a lotus.
The father of all beings, who are His children.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अमृत्युः सर्वदृक् सिंहः सन्धाता सन्धिमान् स्थिरः ।
अजो दुर्मर्षणः शास्ता विश्रुतात्मा सुरारिहा ॥२२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अमृत्युः सर्वदृक् सिंहः सन्धाता सन्धिमान् स्थिरः । | अजो दुर्मर्षणः शास्ता विश्रुतात्मा सुरारिहा ॥२२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
amṛtyuḥ sarvadṛk siṃhaḥ sandhātā sandhimān sthiraḥ,
ajo durmarṣaṇaḥ śāstā viśrutātmā surārihā. (22)
shlokas.meaning_english: Amṛtyuḥ: One who is without death or its cause.; Sarvadṛk: One who sees the Karmas of all Jīvas through His inherent wisdom.; Siṃhaḥ: One who does Hiṃsā (destruction).; Sandhātā: One who unites the Jīvas with the fruits of their actions.; Sandhimān: One who is Himself the enjoyer of the fruits of actions.; Sthiraḥ: One who is always of the same nature.; Ajaḥ: One who goes into the hearts of devotees or destroys Asuras.; Durmarṣaṇaḥ: One whose might the Asuras cannot bear.; Śāstā: One who instructs and directs all through the scriptures.; Viśrutātmā: One who is specially known through signifying terms like Truth, Knowledge.; Surārihā: One who destroys the enemies of Suras or Devas.

padas.meaning: One who is without death or its cause.
One who sees the Karmas of all Jīvas through His inherent wisdom.
One who does Hiṃsā (destruction).
One who unites the Jīvas with the fruits of their actions.
One who is Himself the enjoyer of the fruits of actions.
One who is always of the same nature.
One who goes into the hearts of devotees or destroys Asuras.
One whose might the Asuras cannot bear.
One who instructs and directs all through the scriptures.
One who is specially known through signifying terms like Truth, Knowledge.
One who destroys the enemies of Suras or Devas.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
गुरुर्गुरुतमो धाम सत्यः सत्यपराक्रमः ।
निमिषोऽनिमिषः स्रग्वी वाचस्पतिरुदारधीः ॥२३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: गुरुर्गुरुतमो धाम सत्यः सत्यपराक्रमः । | निमिषोऽनिमिषः स्रग्वी वाचस्पतिरुदारधीः ॥२३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
gurur gurutamo dhāma satyaḥ satyaparākramaḥ,
nimiṣo 'nimiṣaḥ sragvī vācaspatir udāradhīḥ. (23)
shlokas.meaning_english: Guruḥ: The greatest teacher.; Gurutamaḥ: One who is the teacher of all forms of knowledge.; Dhāma: The Supreme Light.; Satyaḥ: One who is embodied as the virtue of truth.; Satyaparākramaḥ: One of unfailing valour.; Nimiṣaḥ: One whose eyelids are closed in Yoga-nidrā.; Animiṣaḥ: One who is ever awake.; Sragvī: One who has the necklace Vaijayantī, strung with the five elements.; Vācaspatir: udāradhīḥ – The master of Vāk (knowledge), of wide intelligence.

padas.meaning: The greatest teacher.
One who is the teacher of all forms of knowledge.
The Supreme Light.
One who is embodied as the virtue of truth.
One of unfailing valour.
One whose eyelids are closed in Yoga-nidrā.
One who is ever awake.
One who has the necklace Vaijayantī, strung with the five elements.
udāradhīḥ – The master of Vāk (knowledge), of wide intelligence.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अग्रणीर्ग्रामणीः श्रीमान् न्यायो नेता समीरणः ।
सहस्रमूर्धा विश्वात्मा सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् ॥२४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अग्रणीर्ग्रामणीः श्रीमान् न्यायो नेता समीरणः । | सहस्रमूर्धा विश्वात्मा सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् ॥२४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
agraṇīr grāmaṇīḥ śrīmān nyāyo netā samīraṇaḥ,
sahasramūrdhā viśvātmā sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt. (24)
shlokas.meaning_english: Agraṇīḥ: One who leads all liberation-seekers to the highest status.; Grāmaṇīḥ: One who has command over the collectivity of all beings.; Śrīmān: One more resplendent than everything.; Nyāyaḥ: The consistency which runs through all ways of knowing.; Netā: One who moves this world of becoming.; Sahasramūrdhā: One with a thousand (innumerable) heads.; Samīraṇaḥ: One who in the form of breath keeps all living beings functioning.; Viśvātmā: The soul of the universe.; Sahasrākṣaḥ: One with a thousand (innumerable) eyes.; Sahasrapāt: One with a thousand (innumerable) legs.

One who has command over the collectivity of all beings.
One more resplendent than everything.
The consistency which runs through all ways of knowing.
One who moves this world of becoming.
One with a thousand (innumerable) heads.
One who in the form of breath keeps all living beings functioning.
The soul of the universe.
One with a thousand (innumerable) eyes.
One with a thousand (innumerable) legs.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
आवर्तनो निवृत्तात्मा संवृतः सम्प्रमर्दनः।
अहः संवर्तको वह्निरनिलो धरणीधरः ॥२५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: आवर्तनो निवृत्तात्मा संवृतः सम्प्रमर्दनः। | अहः संवर्तको वह्निरनिलो धरणीधरः ॥२५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
āvartano nivṛttātmā saṃvṛtaḥ saṃpramardanaḥ,
ahaḥ saṃvartako vahnir anilo dharaṇīdharaḥ. (25)
shlokas.meaning_english: Āvartanaḥ: One who whirls round and round the Samsara-chakra, the wheel of Samsara or worldly existence.; Nivṛttātmā: One whose being is free or untouched by the bondage of Snamsara.; Saṃvṛtaḥ: One who is covered by all-covering Avidyā or ignorance.; Sampramardanaḥ: One who delivers destructive blows on all beings through His Vibhutis (power manifestation like Rudra, Yama etc.).; Ahaḥ: saṃvartakaḥ – The Lord who, as the sun, regulates the succession of day and night.; Vahniḥ: One who as fire carries the offerings made to the Devas in sacrifices.; Anilaḥ: One who has no fixed residence.; Dharaṇī: dharaḥ – One who supports the worlds, Adisesha, elephants of the quarters, etc.

padas.meaning: One who whirls round and round the Samsara-chakra, the wheel of Samsara or worldly existence.
One whose being is free or untouched by the bondage of Snamsara.
One who is covered by all-covering Avidyā or ignorance.
One who delivers destructive blows on all beings through His Vibhutis (power manifestation like Rudra, Yama etc.).
saṃvartakaḥ – The Lord who, as the sun, regulates the succession of day and night.
One who as fire carries the offerings made to the Devas in sacrifices.
One who has no fixed residence.
dharaḥ – One who supports the worlds, Adisesha, elephants of the quarters, etc.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सुप्रसादः प्रसन्नात्मा विश्वधृग्विश्वभुग्विभुः ।
सत्कर्ता सत्कृतः साधुर्जह्नुर्नारायणो नरः ॥२६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सुप्रसादः प्रसन्नात्मा विश्वधृग्विश्वभुग्विभुः । | सत्कर्ता सत्कृतः साधुर्जह्नुर्नारायणो नरः ॥२६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
suprasādaḥ prasannātmā viśvadhṛg viśvabhug vibhuḥ,
satkartā satkṛtaḥ sādhur jahnur nārāyaṇo naraḥ. (26)
shlokas.meaning_english: Suprasādaḥ: One whose Prasada or mercy is uniquely wonderful, because He gives salvation to Sisupala and others who try to harm Him.; Prasannātmā: One whose mind is never contaminated by Rajas or Tamas.; Viśvadhṛg: One who holds the universe by his power.; Viśvabhug: One who eats up or enjoys or protects the worlds.; Vibhuḥ: One who takes various forms.; Satkartā: One who offers benefits.; Satkṛtaḥ: One who is adored even by those who deserve adoration.; Sādhuḥ: One who acts according to justice.; Jahnuḥ: One who dissolves all beings in oneself at the time of dissolution.; Nārāyaṇaḥ: Nara means Ātman. Narayana, that is, one having His residence in all beings.; Naraḥ: He directs everything, the eternal Paramatma is called Nara.

One whose mind is never contaminated by Rajas or Tamas.
One who holds the universe by his power.
One who eats up or enjoys or protects the worlds.
One who takes various forms.
One who offers benefits.
One who is adored even by those who deserve adoration.
One who acts according to justice.
One who dissolves all beings in oneself at the time of dissolution.
Nara means Ātman. Narayana, that is, one having His residence in all beings.
He directs everything, the eternal Paramatma is called Nara.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
असङ्ख्येयोऽप्रमेयात्मा विशिष्टः शिष्टकृच्छुचिः ।
सिद्धार्थः सिद्धसङ्कल्पः सिद्धिदः सिद्धिसाधनः ॥२७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: असङ्ख्येयोऽप्रमेयात्मा विशिष्टः शिष्टकृच्छुचिः । | सिद्धार्थः सिद्धसङ्कल्पः सिद्धिदः सिद्धिसाधनः ॥२७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
asaṅkhyeyo 'prameyātmā viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭakṛc chuciḥ,
siddhārthaḥ siddhasaṅkalpaḥ siddhidaḥ siddhisādhanaḥ. (27)
shlokas.meaning_english: Asaṅkhyeyaḥ: One who has no Sankhya or differences of name and form.; Aprameyātmā: One whose nature cannot be grasped by any of the means of knowledge.; Viśiṣṭaḥ: One who excels everything.; Śiṣṭakṛt: One who commands everything. Or one who protects shishtas or good men.; Suciḥ: Pure; Siddhārthaḥ: One whose object is always fulfilled.; Siddhasaṅkalpaḥ: One whose resolutions are always fulfilled.; Siddhidaḥ: One who bestows Siddhi or fulfillment on all who practise disciplines, in accordance with their eligibility.; Siddhisādhanaḥ: One who brings fulfillment to works that deserve the same.

padas.meaning: One who has no Sankhya or differences of name and form.
One whose nature cannot be grasped by any of the means of knowledge.
One who excels everything.
One who commands everything. Or one who protects shishtas or good men.
Pure
One whose object is always fulfilled.
One whose resolutions are always fulfilled.
One who bestows Siddhi or fulfillment on all who practise disciplines, in accordance with their eligibility.
One who brings fulfillment to works that deserve the same.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वृषाही वृषभो विष्णुर्वृषपर्वा वृषोदरः ।
वर्धनो वर्धमानश्च विविक्तः श्रुतिसागरः ॥२८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: वृषाही वृषभो विष्णुर्वृषपर्वा वृषोदरः । | वर्धनो वर्धमानश्च विविक्तः श्रुतिसागरः ॥२८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vṛṣāhī vṛṣabho viṣṇur vṛṣaparvā vṛṣodaraḥ,
vardhano vardhamānaś ca viviktaḥ śrutisāgaraḥ. (28)
shlokas.meaning_english: Vṛṣāhī: One who is the possessor of Dharma.; Vṛṣābhaḥ: One who showers on the devotees all that they pray for.; Viṣṇuḥ: One who pervades everything.; Vṛṣaparva: One who has given as steps (Parvas), observances of the nature of Dharma, to those who want to attain the supreme state.; Vṛṣodaraḥ: One whose abdomen showers offspring.; Vardhanaḥ: One who increases the ecstasy of His devotees.; Vardhamānaḥ: One who multiplies in the form of the universe.; Viviktaḥ: One who is untouched and unaffected.; Śrutisāgaraḥ: One to whom all the shruti or Vedic words and sentences flow.

padas.meaning: One who is the possessor of Dharma.
One who showers on the devotees all that they pray for.
One who pervades everything.
One who has given as steps (Parvas), observances of the nature of Dharma, to those who want to attain the supreme state.
One whose abdomen showers offspring.
One who increases the ecstasy of His devotees.
One who multiplies in the form of the universe.
One who is untouched and unaffected.
One to whom all the shruti or Vedic words and sentences flow.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः ।
नैकरूपो बृहद्रूपः शिपिविष्टः प्रकाशनः ॥२९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सुभुजो दुर्धरो वाग्मी महेन्द्रो वसुदो वसुः । | नैकरूपो बृहद्रूपः शिपिविष्टः प्रकाशनः ॥२९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
subhujo durddharo vāgmī mahendro vasudo vasuḥ,
naikarūpo bṛhadrūpaḥ śipiviṣṭaḥ prakāśanaḥ. (29)
shlokas.meaning_english: Subhujaḥ: One possessing excellent arms that protect the worlds.; Durdharaḥ: One who holds up the universe – a work which none else can do.; Vāgmi: One from whom the words constituting the Veda come out.; Mahendraḥ: The great Lord, that is, the Supreme Being, who is the God of all gods.; Vasudaḥ: One who bestows riches.; Vasuḥ: One who is himself the Vasu.; Naikarūpaḥ: One who is without an exclusive form.; Bṛhadrūpaḥ: One who has adopted mysterious forms like that of a Boar.; Śipiviṣṭaḥ: Shipi means cow. One who resides in cows as Yajna.; Prakāśanaḥ: One who illumines everthing.

padas.meaning: One possessing excellent arms that protect the worlds.
One who holds up the universe – a work which none else can do.
One from whom the words constituting the Veda come out.
The great Lord, that is, the Supreme Being, who is the God of all gods.
One who bestows riches.
One who is himself the Vasu.
One who is without an exclusive form.
One who has adopted mysterious forms like that of a Boar.
Shipi means cow. One who resides in cows as Yajna.
One who illumines everthing.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ओजस्तेजोद्युतिधरः प्रकाशात्मा प्रतापनः ।
ऋद्धः स्पष्टाक्षरो मन्त्रश्चन्द्रांशुर्भास्करद्युतिः ॥३०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ओजस्तेजोद्युतिधरः प्रकाशात्मा प्रतापनः । | ऋद्धः स्पष्टाक्षरो मन्त्रश्चन्द्रांशुर्भास्करद्युतिः ॥३०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ojas tejo dyutidharaḥ prakāśātmā pratāpanaḥ,
ṛddhaḥ spaṣṭākṣaro mantraś candrāṃśur bhāskaradyutiḥ. (30)
shlokas.meaning_english: Ōjas: tejō-dyuti-dharaḥ – One who is endowed with strength, vigour and brilliance.; Prakāśātmā: One whose form is radiant.; Pratāpanaḥ: One who warms the world through the power manifestations like the Sun.; Jñāna: One who is rich in excellences like Dharma, Gyana (knowledge), Vairagya (renunciation) etc.; Spaṣṭākṣaraḥ: He is so called because  Oṃkāra, the manifesting sound of the Lord, is Spashta or high pitched.; Mantraḥ: One who manifests as the Mantras of the Rk, Sama, Yajus etc., or one who is known through Mantras.; Candrāṃśuḥ: He is called 'Chandramshu' or moonlight because just as the moon-light gives relief to men burnt in the heat of the sun, He gives relief and shelter to those who are subjected to the heat of Samsara.; Bhāskara: dyutiḥ – He who has the effulgence of the sun.

One whose form is radiant.
One who warms the world through the power manifestations like the Sun.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुः शशबिन्दुः सुरेश्वरः ।
औषधं जगतः सेतुः सत्यधर्मपराक्रमः ॥३१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अमृतांशूद्भवो भानुः शशबिन्दुः सुरेश्वरः । | औषधं जगतः सेतुः सत्यधर्मपराक्रमः ॥३१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bhānuḥ śaśabinduḥ sureśvaraḥ,
auṣadhaṃ jagataḥ setuḥ satyadharmaparākramaḥ. (31)
shlokas.meaning_english: Amṛtāṃśūdbhavaḥ: The Paramātman from whom Amrutamshu or the Moon originated at the time of the churning of the Milk- ocean.; Bhānuḥ: One who shines.; Śaśabinduḥ: The word means one who has the mark of the hare, that is the Moon.; Sureśvaraḥ: One who is the Lord of all Devas and those who do good.; Auṣadham: One who is the Aushadha or medicine for the great disease of Samsara.; Jagataḥ setuḥ: One who is the aid to go across the ocean of Samsara.; Satya: dharma-parākramaḥ – One whose excellences like righteousness, omniscience, puissance, etc. are all true.

One who shines.
The word means one who has the mark of the hare, that is the Moon.
One who is the Lord of all Devas and those who do good.
One who is the Aushadha or medicine for the great disease of Samsara.
One who is the aid to go across the ocean of Samsara.
dharma-parākramaḥ – One whose excellences like righteousness, omniscience, puissance, etc. are all true.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भूतभव्यभवन्नाथः पवनः पावनोऽनलः ।
कामहा कामकृत्कान्तः कामः कामप्रदः प्रभुः ॥३२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भूतभव्यभवन्नाथः पवनः पावनोऽनलः । | कामहा कामकृत्कान्तः कामः कामप्रदः प्रभुः ॥३२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
bhūtabhavyabhavannāthaḥ pavanaḥ pāvano 'nalaḥ,
kāmahā kāmakṛt kāntaḥ kāmaḥ kāmapradaḥ prabhuḥ. (32)
shlokas.meaning_english: Bhūta: bhavya-bhavan-nāthaḥ – One who is the master for all the beings of the past, future and present.; Pavanaḥ: One who is the purifier.; Pāvanaḥ: One who causes movement.; Analaḥ: The Jivatma is called Anala because it recognizes Ana or Prāṇa as Himself.; Kāmahā: One who destroys the desire-nature in seekers after liberation.; Kāmakṛt: One who fulfils the wants of pure minded devotees.; Kāntaḥ: One who is extremely beautiful.; Kāmaḥ: One who is sought after by those who desire to attain the four supreme values of life.; Kāmapradaḥ: One who liberally fulfils the desires of devotees.; Prabhuḥ: One who surpasses all.

padas.meaning: bhavya-bhavan-nāthaḥ – One who is the master for all the beings of the past, future and present.
One who is the purifier.
One who causes movement.

One who destroys the desire-nature in seekers after liberation.
One who fulfils the wants of pure minded devotees.
One who is extremely beautiful.
One who is sought after by those who desire to attain the four supreme values of life.
One who liberally fulfils the desires of devotees.
One who surpasses all.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
युगादिकृद्युगावर्तो नैकमायो महाशनः ।
अदृश्यो व्यक्तरूपश्च सहस्रजिदनन्तजित् ॥३३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: युगादिकृद्युगावर्तो नैकमायो महाशनः । | अदृश्यो व्यक्तरूपश्च सहस्रजिदनन्तजित् ॥३३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yugādikṛd yugāvarto naikamāyo mahāśanaḥ,
adṛśyo vyaktarūpaś ca sahasrajid anantajit. (33)
shlokas.meaning_english: Yugādikṛd: One who is the cause of periods of time like Yuga.; Yugāvartaḥ: One who as time causes the repetition of the four Yugas beginning with Satya Yuga.; Naikamāyaḥ: One who can assume numerous forms of Maya, not one only.; Mahāśanaḥ: One who consumes everything at the end of a Kalpa.; Adṛśyaḥ: One who cannot be grasped by any of the five organs of knowledge.; Vyaktarūpaḥ: He is so called because His gross form as universe can be clearly perceived.; Sahasrajit: One who is victorious over innumerable enemies of the Devas in battle.; Anantajit: One who, being endowed with all powers, is victorious at all times over everything.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
इष्टोऽविशिष्टः शिष्टेष्टः शिखण्डी नहुषो वृषः ।
क्रोधहा क्रोधकृत्कर्ता विश्वबाहुर्महीधरः ॥३४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: इष्टोऽविशिष्टः शिष्टेष्टः शिखण्डी नहुषो वृषः । | क्रोधहा क्रोधकृत्कर्ता विश्वबाहुर्महीधरः ॥३४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
iṣṭo 'viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ śikhaṇḍī nahuṣo vṛṣaḥ,
krodhahā krodhakṛt kartā viśvabāhur mahīdharaḥ. (34)
shlokas.meaning_english: Iṣṭaḥ: One who is dear to all because He is of the nature of supreme Bliss.; Aviśiṣṭaḥ: One who resides within all.; Śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ: One who is dear to shishta or Knowing Ones.; Śikhaṇḍī: Sikhanda means feather of a peacock. One who used it as a decoration for His crown when he adopted the form of a cowherd (Gopa).; Nahuṣaḥ: One who binds all beings by Maya the root 'nah' means bondage.; Vṛṣaḥ: One who is of the form of Dharma.; Krōdhahā: One who eradicates anger in virtuous people.; Krōdhakṛt: kartā – One who generates Krodha or anger in evil people.; Viśvabāhuḥ: One who is the support of all or one who has got all beings as His arms.; Mahīdharaḥ: Mahi means both earth and worship. shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अच्युतः प्रथितः प्राणः प्राणदो वासवानुजः ।
अपांनिधिरधिष्ठाानमप्रमत्तः प्रतिष्ठितः ॥३५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अच्युतः प्रथितः प्राणः प्राणदो वासवानुजः । | अपांनिधिरधिष्ठाानमप्रमत्तः प्रतिष्ठितः ॥३५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
acyutaḥ prathitaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇado vāsavānujaḥ,
apāṃ nidhir adhiṣṭhānam apramattaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ. (35)
shlokas.meaning_english: Acyutaḥ: One who is without the six transformations beginning with birth.; Prathitaḥ: One who is famous because of His works like creation of the worlds etc.; Prāṇaḥ: One who as Hiranyagarbha endows all beings with Prana.; Prāṇadaḥ: One who bestows Prāṇa, that is, strength, on Devas and Asuras and also destroys them by withdrawing it.; Vāsavānujaḥ: One who was born as younger brother of Indra (Vasava) in His incarnation as Vamana.; Apāṃ nidhiḥ: The word means collectivity of water or the ocean.; Adhiṣṭhānam: The seat or support for everything.; Apramattaḥ: One who is always vigilant in awarding the fruits of actions to those who are entitled to them.; Pratiṣṭhitaḥ: One who is supported and established in His own greatness.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
स्कन्दः स्कन्दधरो धुर्यो वरदो वायुवाहनः ।
वासुदेवो बृहद्भानुरादिदेवः पुरन्दरः ॥३६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: स्कन्दः स्कन्दधरो धुर्यो वरदो वायुवाहनः । | वासुदेवो बृहद्भानुरादिदेवः पुरन्दरः ॥३६॥

skandaḥ skandadharo dhuryo varado vāyuvāhanaḥ,
vāsudevo bṛhadbhānur ādidevaḥ purandaraḥ. (36)

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अशोकस्तारणस्तारः शूरः शौरिर्जनेश्वरः ।

shlokas.iast_transliteration:
aśokas tāraṇas tāraḥ śūraḥ śaurir janeśvaraḥ,
anukūlaḥ śatāvartaḥ padmī padmanibhekṣaṇaḥ. (37)

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
पद्मनाभोऽरविन्दाक्षः पद्मगर्भः शरीरभृत् ।
महर्द्धिरृद्धो वृद्धात्मा महाक्षो गरुडध्वजः ॥३८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: पद्मनाभोऽरविन्दाक्षः पद्मगर्भः शरीरभृत् । | महर्द्धिरृद्धो वृद्धात्मा महाक्षो गरुडध्वजः ॥३८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
padmanābho 'ravindākṣaḥ padmagarbhaḥ śarīrabhṛt,

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अतुलः शरभो भीमः समयज्ञो हविर्हरिः ।
सर्वलक्षणलक्षण्यो लक्ष्मीवान् समितिञ्जयः ॥३९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अतुलः शरभो भीमः समयज्ञो हविर्हरिः । | सर्वलक्षणलक्षण्यो लक्ष्मीवान् समितिञ्जयः ॥३९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
atulaḥ śarabho bhīmaḥ samayajño havirhariḥ,

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
विक्षरो रोहितो मार्गो हेतुर्दामोदरः सहः ।
महीधरो महाभागो वेगवानमिताशनः ॥४०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: विक्षरो रोहितो मार्गो हेतुर्दामोदरः सहः । | महीधरो महाभागो वेगवानमिताशनः ॥४०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vikṣaro rohito mārgo hetur dāmodaraḥ sahaḥ,

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
उद्भवः क्षोभणो देवः श्रीगर्भः परमेश्वरः ।
करणं कारणं कर्ता विकर्ता गहनो गुहः ॥४१॥

udbhavaḥ kṣobhaṇo devaḥ śrīgarbhaḥ parameśvaraḥ,

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
व्यवसायो व्यवस्थानः संस्थानः स्थानदो ध्रुवः ।
परर्द्धिः परमस्पष्टस्तुष्टः पुष्टः शुभेक्षणः ॥४२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: व्यवसायो व्यवस्थानः संस्थानः स्थानदो ध्रुवः । | परर्द्धिः परमस्पष्टस्तुष्टः पुष्टः शुभेक्षणः ॥४२॥

vyavasāyo vyavasthānaḥ saṃsthānaḥ sthānado dhruvaḥ,

He in whom the orderly regulation of the universe rests.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
रामो विरामो विरजो मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः ।
वीरः शक्तिमतां श्रेष्ठोो धर्मो धर्मविदुत्तमः ॥४३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: रामो विरामो विरजो मार्गो नेयो नयोऽनयः । | वीरः शक्तिमतां श्रेष्ठोो धर्मो धर्मविदुत्तमः ॥४३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
rāmo virāmo virajo mārgo neyo nayo 'nayaḥ,
vīraḥ śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭho dharmo dharmaviduttamaḥ. (43)

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वैकुण्ठः पुरुषः प्राणः प्राणदः प्रणवः पृथुः ।
हिरण्यगर्भः शत्रुघ्नो व्याप्तो वायुरधोक्षजः ॥४४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: वैकुण्ठः पुरुषः प्राणः प्राणदः प्रणवः पृथुः । | हिरण्यगर्भः शत्रुघ्नो व्याप्तो वायुरधोक्षजः ॥४४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ pṛthuḥ,
hiraṇyagarbhaḥ śatrughno vyāpto vāyur adhokṣajaḥ. (44)

He who is the agent of it is Vaikunthah.; Puruṣaḥ: One who existed before everything.; Prāṇaḥ: One who lives as Kshetrajana (knower in the body) or one who functions in the form of vital force called Prāṇa.; Prāṇadaḥ: One who is the giver of life.; Praṇavaḥ: One who is praised or to whom prostration is made with Om.; Pṛthuḥ: One who has expanded himself as the world.; Hiraṇyagarbhaḥ: He who was the cause of the golden-coloured egg out of which Brahma was born.; Śatrughnaḥ: One who destroys the enemies of the Devas.; Vyāptaḥ: One who as the cause pervades all effects.; Vāyuḥ: One who moves towards His devotees.; Adhokṣajaḥ: He is Adhokshaja because he undergoes no degeneration from His original nature.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ऋतुः सुदर्शनः कालः परमेष्ठीी परिग्रहः ।
उग्रः संवत्सरो दक्षो विश्रामो विश्वदक्षिणः ॥४५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ऋतुः सुदर्शनः कालः परमेष्ठीी परिग्रहः । | उग्रः संवत्सरो दक्षो विश्रामो विश्वदक्षिणः ॥४५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ṛtuḥ sudarśanaḥ kālaḥ parameṣṭhī parigrahaḥ,
ugraḥ saṃvatsaro dakṣo viśrāmo viśvadakṣiṇaḥ. (45)
shlokas.meaning_english: Ṛtuḥ: One who is of the nature of Kala (time) which is indicated by the word Ritu or season.; Sudarśanaḥ: One whose Darshana or vision that is knowledge, bestows the most auspicious fruit Mokṣa.; Kālaḥ: One who measures and sets a limit to everything.; Parameṣṭhī: One who dwells in his supreme greatness in the sky of the heart.; Parigrahaḥ: One who, being everywhere, is grasped on all sides by those who seek refuge in Him. विस्तारः स्थावरस्थाणुः प्रमाणं बीजमव्ययम् ।
अर्थोऽनर्थो महाकोशो महाभोगो महाधनः ॥४६॥

shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vistāraḥ sthāvaraḥ sthāṇuḥ pramāṇaṃ bījam avyayam,
artho 'nartho mahākośo mahābhogo mahādhanaḥ. (46)
shlokas.meaning_english: Vistāraḥ: One in whom all the worlds have attained manifestation.; Sthāvaraḥ: sthāṇuḥ – One who is firmly established is Sthavara, and in whom long lasting entities like earth are established in Sthanu. The Lord is both these.; Pramāṇaṃ: One who is of the nature of pure consciousness.; Bījamavyayam: One who is the seed or cause of Samsara without Himself undergoing any change.; Arthaḥ: One who is sought (Arthita) by all, as He is of the nature of bliss.; Anarthaḥ: One who, being self-fulfilled, has no other Artha or end to seek.; Mahākōśaḥ: One who has got as His covering the great Koshas like Annamaya, Prāṇamaya etc.; Mahābhōgaḥ: One who has Bliss as the great source of enjoyment.; Mahādhanaḥ: One who has got the whole universe as the wealth (Dhana) for His enjoyment.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अनिर्विण्णः स्थविष्ठोोऽभूर्धर्मयूपो महामखः ।

anirviṇṇaḥ sthaviṣṭho 'bhūr dharmayūpo mahāmakhaḥ,

shlokas.meaning_english: Anirviṇṇaḥ: One who is never heedless, because He is ever self- fulfilled.; Sthaviṣṭhaḥ: One of huge proportions, because He is in the form of cosmic person.; Abhūḥ: One without birth. Or one has no existence.; Dharma: yūpaḥ – The sacrificial post for Dharmas, that is, one to whom all the forms of Dharma, which are His own form of worship, are attached, just as a sacrificial animal is attached to a Yupa or a sacrificial post.; Mahāmakhaḥ: One by offering sacrifices to whom, those sacrifices deserve to be called great, because they would give the fruit of Nirvana.; Nakṣatra: nemiḥ – The heart of all nakshatras.; Nakṣatrī: He is in the form of the nakshatra, Moon.; Kṣamaḥ: One who is clever in everything.; Kṣāmaḥ: One who remains in the state of pure self after all the modifications of the mind have dwindled.; Samīhanaḥ: One who exerts well for creation, etc.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यज्ञ इज्यो महेज्यश्च क्रतुः सत्रं सतां गतिः ।

yajña ijyo mahejyaś ca kratuḥ satraṃ satāṃ gatiḥ,

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सुव्रतः सुमुखः सूक्ष्मः सुघोषः सुखदः सुहृत् ।

Dharma and Adharma, He performs Dharma in order to keep up the traditions in respect of it.; Dharmī: One who upholds Dharma.; Sat: The Parabrahman who is of the nature of truth.; Asat: As the Aparabrahma has manifested as the world He is called Asat (not having reality).; Kṣaram: All beings subjected to change.; Akṣaram: The changeless one.; Avijñātā: One who is without the attributes of a Jiva or vigyata like sense of agency, etc.; Sahasrāṃśuḥ: One with numerous rays, that is the Sun.; Vidhātā: One who is the unique support of all agencies like Ananta who bear the whole universe.; Kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ: One who is of the nature of consciousness.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
गभस्तिनेमिः सत्त्वस्थः सिंहो भूतमहेश्वरः ।
आदिदेवो महादेवो देवेशो देवभृद्गुरुः ॥५२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: गभस्तिनेमिः सत्त्वस्थः सिंहो भूतमहेश्वरः । | आदिदेवो महादेवो देवेशो देवभृद्गुरुः ॥५२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
gabhastinemiḥ sattvasthaḥ siṃho bhūtamaheśvaraḥ,
ādidevo mahādevo deveśo devabhṛd guruḥ. (52)
shlokas.meaning_english: Gabhastinemiḥ: He who dwells in the middle of Gabhasti or rays as the Sun.; Sattvasthaḥ: One who dwells specially in sattvaguna, which is luminous by nature.; Simhaḥ: One who has irresistible power like a lion.; Bhūtamaheśvaraḥ: The supreme Lord of all beings.; Ādidevaḥ: He who is the first of all beings.; Mahādevaḥ: One whose greatness consists in His supreme self- knowledge.; Deveśaḥ: One who is the lord of all Devas, being the most important among them.; Devabhṛd: guruḥ – Indra who governs the Devas is Devabhrut. The Lord is even that Indra's controller (Guru).

padas.meaning: He who dwells in the middle of Gabhasti or rays as the Sun.
One who dwells specially in sattvaguna, which is luminous by nature.
One who has irresistible power like a lion.
The supreme Lord of all beings.
He who is the first of all beings.
One whose greatness consists in His supreme self- knowledge.
One who is the lord of all Devas, being the most important among them.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
उत्तरो गोपतिर्गोप्ता ज्ञानगम्यः पुरातनः ।
शरीरभूतभृद्भोक्ता कपीन्द्रो भूरिदक्षिणः ॥५३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: उत्तरो गोपतिर्गोप्ता ज्ञानगम्यः पुरातनः । | शरीरभूतभृद्भोक्ता कपीन्द्रो भूरिदक्षिणः ॥५३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
uttaro gopatiḥ goptā jñānagamyaḥ purātanaḥ,
śarīrabhūtabhṛd bhoktā kapīndro bhūridakṣiṇaḥ. (53)
shlokas.meaning_english: Uttaraḥ: One who is Uttirna or liberated from Samsara.; Gōpatiḥ: Krishna who tends the cattle in the form of a Gopa. One who is the master of the earth.; Gōptā: One who is the protector of all beings.; Jñānagamyaḥ: The Lord cannot be known through Karma or a combination of Karma and Jñāna.; Purātanaḥ: One who is not limited by time and who existed before anything else.; Śarīrabhūtabhṛd: One who is the master of the five Bhutas (elements) of which the body is made.; Bhōktā: One who protects. Or one who is the enjoyer of infinite bliss.; Kapīndraḥ: Kapi means Varah (boar). The word means, the Lord who is Indra and also one who manifested as Varaha or the Boar in one of the incarnations. Or it signifies His Rama incarnation in which He played the role of the master of the monkeys.; Bhūridakṣiṇaḥ: One to whom numerous Dakshinas or votive offerings are made in Yajnas.

padas.meaning: One who is Uttirna or liberated from Samsara.
Krishna who tends the cattle in the form of a Gopa. One who is the master of the earth.
One who is the protector of all beings.

One who is not limited by time and who existed before anything else.
One who is the master of the five Bhutas (elements) of which the body is made.
One who protects. Or one who is the enjoyer of infinite bliss.

One to whom numerous Dakshinas or votive offerings are made in Yajnas.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सोमपोऽमृतपः सोमः पुरुजित्पुरुसत्तमः ।
विनयो जयः सत्यसन्धो दाशार्हः सात्वताम्पतिः ॥५४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सोमपोऽमृतपः सोमः पुरुजित्पुरुसत्तमः । | विनयो जयः सत्यसन्धो दाशार्हः सात्वताम्पतिः ॥५४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
somapo 'mṛtapaḥ somaḥ purujit purusattamaḥ,
vinayo jayaḥ satyasandho dāśārhaḥ sātvatāṃ patiḥ. (54)
shlokas.meaning_english: Sōmapaḥ: One who drinks the Soma in all Yajnas in the form of the Devata.; Amṛtapaḥ: One who drinks the drink of immortal Bliss which is of one's own nature.; Sōmaḥ: One who as the moon invigorates the plants.; Purujit: One who gains victory over numerous people.; Puruṣhottamaḥ: As His form is of cosmic dimension He is Puru or great, and as He is the most important of all, He is Sattama.; Vinayaḥ: One who inflicts Vinaya or punishment on evil ones.; Jayaḥ: One who is victorious over all beings.; Satyasandhaḥ: One whose 'Sandha' or resolve becomes always true.; Dāśārhaḥ: Dasha means charitable offering. Therefore, He to whom charitable offerings deserve to be made.; Sātvatāṃ: patiḥ – 'Satvatam' is the name of a Tantra. So the one who gave it out or commented upon it.

padas.meaning: One who drinks the Soma in all Yajnas in the form of the Devata.
One who drinks the drink of immortal Bliss which is of one's own nature.
One who as the moon invigorates the plants.
One who gains victory over numerous people.
As His form is of cosmic dimension He is Puru or great, and as He is the most important of all, He is Sattama.
One who inflicts Vinaya or punishment on evil ones.
One who is victorious over all beings.
One whose 'Sandha' or resolve becomes always true.
Dasha means charitable offering. Therefore, He to whom charitable offerings deserve to be made.
patiḥ – 'Satvatam' is the name of a Tantra. So the one who gave it out or commented upon it.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
जीवो विनयिता साक्षी मुकुन्दोऽमितविक्रमः ।
अम्भोनिधिरनन्तात्मा महोदधिशयोऽन्तकः ॥५५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: जीवो विनयिता साक्षी मुकुन्दोऽमितविक्रमः । | अम्भोनिधिरनन्तात्मा महोदधिशयोऽन्तकः ॥५५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
jīvo vinayitā sākṣī mukundo 'mitavikramaḥ,
ambhonidhir anantātmā mahodadhiśayo 'ntakaḥ. (55)
shlokas.meaning_english: Jīvaḥ: One who as the Kshetragya or knower of the field or the body, is associated with the Prāṇas.; Vinayitā: sākṣī – One who witnesses the Vinayita or worshipful attitude of all devotees.; Mukundaḥ: One who bestows Mukti or Liberation.; Amitavikramaḥ: One whose three strides were limitless.; Ambhōnidhiḥ: One in whom the Ambas or all beings from Devas down dwell.; Anantātmā: One who cannot be determined by space, time and causation.; Mahōdadhi: śayaḥ – One who lies in the water of Cosmic Dissolution into which all entities in the universe have been dissolved.; Antakaḥ: One who brings about the end of all beings.

padas.meaning: One who as the Kshetragya or knower of the field or the body, is associated with the Prāṇas.

One who bestows Mukti or Liberation.
One whose three strides were limitless.
One in whom the Ambas or all beings from Devas down dwell.
One who cannot be determined by space, time and causation.
śayaḥ – One who lies in the water of Cosmic Dissolution into which all entities in the universe have been dissolved.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अजो महार्हः स्वाभाव्यो जितामित्रः प्रमोदनः ।
आनन्दो नन्दनो नन्दः सत्यधर्मा त्रिविक्रमः ॥५६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अजो महार्हः स्वाभाव्यो जितामित्रः प्रमोदनः । | आनन्दो नन्दनो नन्दः सत्यधर्मा त्रिविक्रमः ॥५६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ajo mahārhaḥ svābhāvyo jitāmitraḥ pramodanaḥ,
ānando nandano nandaḥ satyadharmā trivikramaḥ. (56)
shlokas.meaning_english: Ajaḥ: 'A' means Mahavishnu. So the word means one who is born of Vishnu i.e. Kama Deva.; Mahārhaḥ: One who is fit for worship.; Svābhāvyaḥ: Being eternally perfect He is naturally without a beginning.; Jitāmitraḥ: One who has conquered the inner enemies like attachment, anger, etc. as also external enemies like Ravana, Kumbhakarna etc.; Pramōdanaḥ: One who is always joyous as He is absorbed in immortal Bliss.; Ānandaḥ: One whose form is Ananda or Bliss.; Nandanaḥ: One who gives delight.; Nandaḥ: One endowed with all perfections.; Satyadharmā: One whose knowledge and other attributes are true.; Trivikramaḥ: One whose three strides covered the whole world.

One whose form is Ananda or Bliss.
One who gives delight.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
महर्षिः कपिलाचार्यः कृतज्ञो मेदिनीपतिः ।
त्रिपदस्त्रिदशाध्यक्षो महाशङ्गः कृतान्तकृत् ॥५७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: महर्षिः कपिलाचार्यः कृतज्ञो मेदिनीपतिः । | त्रिपदस्त्रिदशाध्यक्षो महाशङ्गः कृतान्तकृत् ॥५७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
maharṣiḥ kapilācāryaḥ kṛtajño medinīpatiḥ,
tripadas tridaśādhyakṣo mahāśṛṅgaḥ kṛtāntakṛt. (57)
shlokas.meaning_english: Maharṣiḥ Kapilācāryaḥ: Kapila is called Maharshi because he was master of all the Vedas.; Kṛtajñaḥ: Kruta means the world because it is of the nature of an effect.; Medinīpatiḥ: One who is the Lord of the earth.; Tripadaḥ: One having three strides.; Tridaśādhyakṣaḥ: One who is the witness of the three states of waking, dream and sleep, which spring from the influence of the Gunas.; Mahāśṛṅgaḥ: One with a great horn.; Kṛtānta: kṛt – One who brings about the destruction of the Kṛta or the manifested condition of the universe.

Kruta means the world because it is of the nature of an effect.
One who is the Lord of the earth.
One having three strides.
One who is the witness of the three states of waking, dream and sleep, which spring from the influence of the Gunas.
One with a great horn.
kṛt – One who brings about the destruction of the Kṛta or the manifested condition of the universe.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
महावराहो गोविन्दः सुषेणः कनकाङ्गदी ।
गुह्यो गभीरो गहनो गुप्तश्चक्रगदाधरः ॥५८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: महावराहो गोविन्दः सुषेणः कनकाङ्गदी । | गुह्यो गभीरो गहनो गुप्तश्चक्रगदाधरः ॥५८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
mahāvarāho govindaḥ suṣeṇaḥ kanakāṅgadī,
guhyo gabhīro gahano guptaś cakragadādharaḥ. (58)
shlokas.meaning_english: Mahā: varāhaḥ – The great Cosmic Boar.; Gōvindaḥ: 'Go' means Words, that is the Vedic sentences. He who is known by them is Gōvindaḥ.; Suṣeṇaḥ: One who has got about Him an armed guard in the shape of His eternal associates.; Kanakāṅgadī: One who has Angadas (armlets) made of gold.; Guhyaḥ: One who is to be known by the Guhya or the esoteric knowledge conveyed by the Upanishads. Or one who is hidden in the Guha or heart.; Gabhīraḥ: One who is of profound majesty because of attributes like omniscience, lordliness, strength, prowess, etc.; Gahanaḥ: One who could be entered into only with great difficulty. shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वेधाः स्वाङ्गोऽजितः कृष्णो दृढः सङ्कर्षणोऽच्युतः ।
वरुणो वारुणो वृक्षः पुष्कराक्षो महामनाः ॥५९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: वेधाः स्वाङ्गोऽजितः कृष्णो दृढः सङ्कर्षणोऽच्युतः । | वरुणो वारुणो वृक्षः पुष्कराक्षो महामनाः ॥५९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vedhāḥ svāṅgo 'jitaḥ kṛṣṇo dṛḍhaḥ saṅkarṣaṇo 'cyutaḥ,
varuṇo vāruṇo vṛkṣaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāmanāḥ. (59)
shlokas.meaning_english: Vedhāḥ: One who does Vidhana or regulation.; Svāṅgaḥ: One who is oneself the participant in accomplishing works.; Ajitaḥ: One who has not been conquered by anyone in His various incarnations.; Kṛṣṇaḥ: One who is known as Krishna-dvaipayana.; Dṛḍhaḥ: One whose nature and capacity know no decay.; Saṅkarṣaṇo: acyutaḥ – Sankarshana is one who attracts to oneself all beings at the time of cosmic Dissolution and Acyuta is one who knows no fall from His real nature. Or one who has eyes resembling the lotus.; Mahāmanāḥ: One who fulfils the three functions of creation, sustentation and dissolution of the universe by the mind alone.

One who is oneself the participant in accomplishing works.
One who has not been conquered by anyone in His various incarnations.
One who is known as Krishna-dvaipayana.
One whose nature and capacity know no decay.

One who is unshakable like a tree.

One who fulfils the three functions of creation, sustentation and dissolution of the universe by the mind alone.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भगवान् भगहाऽऽनन्दी वनमाली हलायुधः ।
आदित्यो ज्योतिरादित्यः सहिष्णुर्गतिसत्तमः ॥६०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भगवान् भगहाऽऽनन्दी वनमाली हलायुधः । | आदित्यो ज्योतिरादित्यः सहिष्णुर्गतिसत्तमः ॥६०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
bhagavān bhagahānandī vanamālī halāyudhaḥ,
ādityo jyotir ādityaḥ sahiṣṇur gatisattamaḥ. (60)

padas.meaning: The origin, dissolution, the bondage and salvation of creatures, knowledge, ignorance – one who knows all these is Bhagavan.
One who withdraws the six divine attributes (bhaga) into Himself at dissolution.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सुधन्वा खण्डपरशुर्दारुणो द्रविणप्रदः ।
दिवस्पृक् सर्वदृग्व्यासो वाचस्पतिरयोनिजः ॥६१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सुधन्वा खण्डपरशुर्दारुणो द्रविणप्रदः । | दिवस्पृक् सर्वदृग्व्यासो वाचस्पतिरयोनिजः ॥६१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sudhanvā khaṇḍaparaśur dāruṇo draviṇapradaḥ,
divaḥspṛk sarvadṛg vyāso vācaspatir ayonijaḥ. (61)
shlokas.meaning_english: Sudhanvā: One who has got as His weapon the bow named Saranga of great excellence.; Khaṇda: paraśuḥ – The battle-axe that destroys enemies.; Dāruṇaḥ: One who is harsh and merciless to those who are on the evil path.; Draviṇapradaḥ: One who bestows the desired wealth on devotees.; Divah: spṛk – One who touches the heavens.; Sarvadṛg: vyāsaḥ – One whose comprehension includes everything in its ambit.; Vācaspatirayōnijaḥ: The Lord is Vachaspati because He is the master of all learning. He is Ayonija because He was not born of a mother. This forms a noun in combination with the attribute.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
त्रिसामा सामगः साम निर्वाणं भेषजं भिषक् ।
संन्यासकृच्छमः शान्तो निष्ठाा शान्तिः परायणम् ॥६२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: त्रिसामा सामगः साम निर्वाणं भेषजं भिषक् । | संन्यासकृच्छमः शान्तो निष्ठाा शान्तिः परायणम् ॥६२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
trisāmā sāmagaḥ sāma nirvāṇaṃ bheṣajaṃ bhiṣak,
saṃnyāsakṛc chamaḥ śānto niṣṭhā śāntiḥ parāyaṇam. (62)
shlokas.meaning_english: Trisāmā: One who is praised by the chanters of Sama-gana through the three Samas known as Devavratam.; Sāmagaḥ: One who chants the Sama-gana.; Sāma: Among the Vedas, I am Sama Veda.; Nirvāṇaṃ: That in which all miseries cease and which is of the nature of supreme bliss.; Bheṣajaṃ: The medicine for the disease of Samsara.; Bhiṣak: The Lord is called Bhishak or physician.; Saṃnyāsakṛt: One who instituted the fourth Ashrama of Sanyasa for the attainment of Mokṣa.; Samaḥ: One who has ordained the pacification of the mind as the most important discipline for Sannyasins (ascetics).; Sāntaḥ: The peaceful, being without interest in pleasures of the world.; Niṣṭhā: One in whom all beings remain in abeyance at the time of Pralaya.; Śāntiḥ: One in whom there is complete erasing of Avidyā or ignorance. shlokas.full_sanskrit:
शुभाङ्गः शान्तिदः स्रष्टा कुमुदः कुवलेशयः ।
गोहितो गोपतिर्गोप्ता वृषभाक्षो वृषप्रियः ॥६३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: शुभाङ्गः शान्तिदः स्रष्टा कुमुदः कुवलेशयः । | गोहितो गोपतिर्गोप्ता वृषभाक्षो वृषप्रियः ॥६३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śubhāṅgaḥ śāntidaḥ sraṣṭā kumudaḥ kuvaleśayaḥ,
gohito gopatiḥ goptā vṛṣabhākṣo vṛṣapriyaḥ. (63)
shlokas.meaning_english: Śubhāṅgaḥ: One with a handsome form.; Śāntidaḥ: One who bestows shanti, that is, a state of freedom from attachment, antagonism, etc.; Sraṣṭā: One who brought forth everything at the start of the creative cycle.; Kumudaḥ: 'Ku' means the earth. One who delights in it.; Kuvaleśayaḥ: 'Ku' means earth. That which surrounds it is water, so 'Kuvala' means water. One who lies in water is Kuvalesaya. 'Kuvala' also means the underside of serpents. One who lies on a serpent, known as Adisesha, is Kuvalesaya.; Gōhitaḥ: One who protected the cows by uplifting the mount Govardhana in His incarnation as Krishna.; Gōpatiḥ: The Lord of the earth is Vishnu.; Gōptā: One who is the protector of the earth. Or one who hides Himself by His Maya.; Vṛṣabhākṣaḥ: One whose eyes shower all desired objects on devotees; one whose glance is full of Dharma.; Vṛṣ apriyaḥ: One to whom Vṛṣa or Dharma is dear.

One who brought forth everything at the start of the creative cycle.
'Ku' means the earth. One who delights in it.
