One who is the protector of the earth. Or one who hides Himself by His Maya.
One whose eyes shower all desired objects on devotees; one whose glance is full of Dharma.
One to whom Vṛṣa or Dharma is dear.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अनिवर्ती निवृत्तात्मा सङ्क्षेप्ता क्षेमकृच्छिवः ।
श्रीवत्सवक्षाः श्रीवासः श्रीपतिः श्रीमतांवरः ॥६४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अनिवर्ती निवृत्तात्मा सङ्क्षेप्ता क्षेमकृच्छिवः । | श्रीवत्सवक्षाः श्रीवासः श्रीपतिः श्रीमतांवरः ॥६४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
anivartī nivṛttātmā saṃkṣeptā kṣemakṛc chivaḥ,
śrīvatsavakṣāḥ śrīvāsaḥ śrīpatiḥ śrīmatāṃ varaḥ. (64)
shlokas.meaning_english: Anivartī: One who never retreats in the battle with Asuras. Or one who, being devoted to Dharma, never abandons it.; Nivṛttātmā: One whose mind is naturally withdrawn from the objects of senses.; Saṃkṣeptā: One who at the time of cosmic dissolution contracts the expansive universe into a subtle state.; Kṣemakṛt: One who gives Kshema or protection to those that go to him.; Śivaḥ: One who purifies everyone by the very utterance of His name.; Śrīvatsavakṣāḥ: One on whose chest there is a mark called Śrīvatsa.; Śrīvāsaḥ: One on whose chest Śrīdevī always dwells.; Śrīpatiḥ: One whom at the time of the churning of the Milk ocean Shridevi chose as her consort, rejecting all other Devas and Asuras. Or Shri mean supreme Cosmic Power. The Lord is the master of that Power.; Śrīmatāṃ: varaḥ – One who is supreme over all deities like Brahma who are endowed with power and wealth of the Vedas.

padas.meaning: One who never retreats in the battle with Asuras. Or one who, being devoted to Dharma, never abandons it.
One whose mind is naturally withdrawn from the objects of senses.
One who at the time of cosmic dissolution contracts the expansive universe into a subtle state.
One who gives Kshema or protection to those that go to him.

varaḥ – One who is supreme over all deities like Brahma who are endowed with power and wealth of the Vedas.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः ।
श्रीधरः श्रीकरः श्रेयः श्रीमाँल्लोकत्रयाश्रयः ॥६५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: श्रीदः श्रीशः श्रीनिवासः श्रीनिधिः श्रीविभावनः । | श्रीधरः श्रीकरः श्रेयः श्रीमाँल्लोकत्रयाश्रयः ॥६५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śrīdaḥ śrīśaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ śrīnidhiḥ śrīvibhāvanaḥ,
śrīdharaḥ śrīkaraḥ śreyaḥ śrīmān lokatrayāśrayaḥ. (65)
shlokas.meaning_english: Śrīdaḥ: One who bestows prosperity on devotees.; Śrīśaḥ: One who is Lord of the Goddess Shri.; Śrīnivāsaḥ: Shri here denotes men with Shri, that is, virtue and power. He who dwells in such men is Shrinivasa.; Śrīnidhiḥ: One who is the seat of all Shri, that is, virtues and powers.; Śrīvibhāvanaḥ: One who grants every form of prosperity and virtue according to their Karma.; Śrīdharaḥ: One who bears on His chest Shri who is the mother of all.; Śrīkaraḥ: One who makes devotees – those who praise, think about Him and worship Him- into virtuous and powerful beings.; Śreyaḥ: 'Shreyas' means the attainment of what is un-decaying good and happiness. Such a state is the nature of the Lord.; Śrīmān: One in whom there are all forms of Shri that is power, virtue, beauty, etc.; Lōkatrayāśrayaḥ: One who is the support of all the three worlds.

One who is Lord of the Goddess Shri.

One who is the seat of all Shri, that is, virtues and powers.
One who grants every form of prosperity and virtue according to their Karma.
One who bears on His chest Shri who is the mother of all.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
स्वक्षः स्वङ्गः शतानन्दो नन्दिर्ज्योतिर्गणेश्वरः ।
विजितात्माऽविधेयात्मा सत्कीर्तिश्छिन्नसंशयः ॥६६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: स्वक्षः स्वङ्गः शतानन्दो नन्दिर्ज्योतिर्गणेश्वरः । | विजितात्माऽविधेयात्मा सत्कीर्तिश्छिन्नसंशयः ॥६६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
svakṣaḥ svaṅgaḥ śatānando nandir jyotirgaṇeśvaraḥ,
vijitātmā vidheyātmā satkīrtiś chinnasaṃśayaḥ. (66)
shlokas.meaning_english: Svakṣaḥ: One who's Akshas (eyes) are handsome like lotus flowers.; Svaṅgaḥ: One whose limbs are beautiful.; Śatānandaḥ: One who is non-dual and is of the nature of supreme bliss.; Nandiḥ: One who is of the nature of supreme Bliss.; Jyōtir: gaṇeśvaraḥ – One who is the Lord of the stars, that is, Jyotirgana.; Vijitātmā: One who has conquered the Atma that is the mind.; Vidheyātmā: One whose Self is perfectly disciplined/governed.; Satkīrtiḥ: One whose fame is of the nature of truth.; Chinna: saṃśayaḥ – One who has no doubts, as everything is clear to him like a fruit in the palm.

padas.meaning: One who's Akshas (eyes) are handsome like lotus flowers.
One whose limbs are beautiful.
One who is non-dual and is of the nature of supreme bliss.
One who is of the nature of supreme Bliss.
gaṇeśvaraḥ – One who is the Lord of the stars, that is, Jyotirgana.
One who has conquered the Atma that is the mind.
One whose Self is perfectly disciplined/governed.
One whose fame is of the nature of truth.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
उदीर्णः सर्वतश्चक्षुरनीशः शाश्वतस्थिरः ।
भूशयो भूषणो भूतिर्विशोकः शोकनाशनः ॥६७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: उदीर्णः सर्वतश्चक्षुरनीशः शाश्वतस्थिरः । | भूशयो भूषणो भूतिर्विशोकः शोकनाशनः ॥६७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
udīrṇaḥ sarvataś cakṣur anīśaḥ śāśvatasthiraḥ,
bhūśayo bhūṣaṇo bhūtir viśokaḥ śokanāśanaḥ. (67)
shlokas.meaning_english: Udīrṇaḥ: He who is superior to all beings.; Sarvataḥ: cakṣuḥ – One who, being of the nature of pure consciousness, can see everthing in all directions.; Anīśaḥ: One who cannot have anyone to lord over him.; Śāśvata: sthiraḥ – One, who though eternal is also unchanging.; Bhūśayaḥ: One who, while seeking the means to cross over to Lanka, had to sleep on the ground of the sea-beach.; Bhūṣaṇaḥ: One who adorned the earth by manifesting as various incarnations.; Bhūtiḥ: One who is the abode or the essence of everthing, or is the source of all glorious manifestations.; Viśōkaḥ: One who, being of the nature of bliss, is free from all sorrow.; Śōkanāśanaḥ: One who effaces the sorrows of devotees even by mere remembrance.

One who, being of the nature of bliss, is free from all sorrow.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अर्चिष्मानर्चितः कुम्भो विशुद्धात्मा विशोधनः ।
अनिरुद्धोऽप्रतिरथः प्रद्युम्नोऽमितविक्रमः ॥६८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अर्चिष्मानर्चितः कुम्भो विशुद्धात्मा विशोधनः । | अनिरुद्धोऽप्रतिरथः प्रद्युम्नोऽमितविक्रमः ॥६८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
arciṣmān arcitaḥ kumbho viśuddhātmā viśodhanaḥ,

shlokas.meaning_english: Arciṣmān: He by whose rays of light (Arciṣ), the sun, the moon and other luminaries are endowed with brilliance.; Arcitaḥ: One who is worshipped by Brahma and other Devas who are themselves objects of worship in all the worlds.; Kumbhaḥ: He who contains everything within Himself, as in a pot.; Viśuddhātmā: Being above the three Guṇas – Sattva, Rajas and Tamas – the Lord is pure spirit and is also free from all impurities.; Viśodhanaḥ: One who destroys all sins by mere remembrance.; Aniruddhaḥ: The last of the four Vyūhas – Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna and Aniruddha. One whose Dyumna (wealth) is of a superior and sacred order. Or one of the four Vyūhas.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
कालनेमिनिहा वीरः शौरिः शूरजनेश्वरः ।
त्रिलोकात्मा त्रिलोकेशः केशवः केशिहा हरिः ॥६९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: कालनेमिनिहा वीरः शौरिः शूरजनेश्वरः । | त्रिलोकात्मा त्रिलोकेशः केशवः केशिहा हरिः ॥६९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
kālaneminihā vīraḥ śauriḥ śūrajaneśvaraḥ,
trilokātmā trilokeśaḥ keśavaḥ keśihā hariḥ. (69)
shlokas.meaning_english: Kālanemi: nihā – One who destroyed the Asura named Kālanemi.; Vīraḥ: One who is courageous and valiant.; Śauriḥ: One who was born in the clan of Śūra, as Kṛṣṇa.; Śūrajaneśvaraḥ: One who by his overwhelming prowess controls even great powers like Indra and others.; Trilokātmā: One who, in his capacity as the inner pervader, is the soul of the three worlds.; Trilokeśaḥ: One under whose guidance and command everything in the three worlds is functioning.; Keśavaḥ: By Keśa is meant the rays of light spreading within the orbit of the sun; the Lord is thus their source.; Keśihā: One who destroyed the Asura named Keśi.; Hariḥ: One who destroys Saṃsāra – entanglement in the cycle of birth and death – along with ignorance, its cause.

shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: कामदेवः कामपालः कामी कान्तः कृतागमः । | अनिर्देश्यवपुर्विष्णुर्वीरोऽनन्तो धनञ्जयः ॥७०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
kāmadevaḥ kāmapālaḥ kāmī kāntaḥ kṛtāgamaḥ,

shlokas.full_sanskrit:

shlokas.iast_transliteration:

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
महाक्रमो महाकर्मा महातेजा महोरगः ।
महाक्रतुर्महायज्वा महायज्ञो महाहविः ॥७२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: महाक्रमो महाकर्मा महातेजा महोरगः । | महाक्रतुर्महायज्वा महायज्ञो महाहविः ॥७२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
mahākramo mahākarmā mahātejā mahoragaḥ,
mahākratur mahāyajvā mahāyajño mahāhaviḥ. (72)
shlokas.meaning_english: Mahākramaḥ: One with enormous strides. May Viṣṇu with enormous strides bestow on us happiness.; Mahākarmā: One who performs great works such as the creation of the world.; Mahātejāḥ: He from whose brilliance the sun and other luminaries derive their brilliance.; Mahoragaḥ: He who is also the great serpent (Ādiśeṣa).; Mahākratuḥ: He who is the great Kratu (sacrifice).; Mahāyajvā: One who is great and performs sacrifices for the good of the world.; Mahāyajñaḥ: He who is the great Yajña (sacrifice) itself.; Mahāhaviḥ: The whole universe conceived as Brahman and offered as sacrificial oblation (Havis) into the fire of the Self, which is Brahman.

One who performs great works such as the creation of the world.
He from whose brilliance the sun and other luminaries derive their brilliance.
He who is also the great serpent (Ādiśeṣa).
He who is the great Kratu (sacrifice).
One who is great and performs sacrifices for the good of the world.
He who is the great Yajña (sacrifice) itself.
The whole universe conceived as Brahman and offered as sacrificial oblation (Havis) into the fire of the Self, which is Brahman.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः ।
पूर्णः पूरयिता पुण्यः पुण्यकीर्तिरनामयः ॥७३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: स्तव्यः स्तवप्रियः स्तोत्रं स्तुतिः स्तोता रणप्रियः । | पूर्णः पूरयिता पुण्यः पुण्यकीर्तिरनामयः ॥७३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
stavyaḥ stavapriyaḥ stotraṃ stutiḥ stotā raṇapriyaḥ,
pūrṇaḥ pūrayitā puṇyaḥ puṇyakīrtir anāmayaḥ. (73)
shlokas.meaning_english: Stavyaḥ: One who is the object of laudations by all, but who Himself never praises any other being.; Stava: priyaḥ – One who is pleased with hymns of praise.; Stotraṃ: A Stotra – a hymn proclaiming the glory, attributes and names of the Lord.; Stutiḥ: Praise itself; the act of glorification.; Stotā: One who, being all-formed, is also the person who sings the hymn of praise.; Raṇapriyaḥ: One who is fond of battle for the protection of the world, ever bearing the discus Sudarśana, the mace Kaumodakī, the bow Śārṅga, the sword Nandaka and the conch Pāñcajanya.; Pūrṇaḥ: One who is self-fulfilled, being the source of all powers and excellences.; Pūrayitā: One who is not only self-fulfilled but gives all fulfillments to others.; Puṇyaḥ: One by merely hearing about whom all sins are erased.; Puṇyakīrtiḥ: One of holy fame, whose excellences confer great merit on others.; Anāmayaḥ: One who is not afflicted by any disease arising from internal or external causes.

padas.meaning: One who is the object of laudations by all, but who Himself never praises any other being.
priyaḥ – One who is pleased with hymns of praise.
A Stotra – a hymn proclaiming the glory, attributes and names of the Lord.
Praise itself; the act of glorification.
One who, being all-formed, is also the person who sings the hymn of praise.
One who is fond of battle for the protection of the world, ever bearing the discus Sudarśana, the mace Kaumodakī, the bow Śārṅga, the sword Nandaka and the conch Pāñcajanya.

One who is not only self-fulfilled but gives all fulfillments to others.
One by merely hearing about whom all sins are erased.
One of holy fame, whose excellences confer great merit on others.
One who is not afflicted by any disease arising from internal or external causes.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
मनोजवस्तीर्थकरो वसुरेता वसुप्रदः ।
वसुप्रदो वासुदेवो वसुर्वसुमना हविः ॥७४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: मनोजवस्तीर्थकरो वसुरेता वसुप्रदः । | वसुप्रदो वासुदेवो वसुर्वसुमना हविः ॥७४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
manojavastīrthakaraḥ vasuretas vasupradaḥ,
vasuprado vāsudevo vasur vasumānā haviḥ. (74)
shlokas.meaning_english: Manojavaḥ: One who, being all-pervading, is said to be endowed with speed like that of the mind.; Tīrthakaraḥ: Tīrtha means Vidyā, a branch of knowledge or skill. One who is the source of all sacred knowledge.; Vasu: retāḥ – He whose Retas (creative essence) is golden (Vasu) in nature.; Vasupradaḥ (1): One who gladly bestows wealth in abundance; the true master of all wealth.; Vasupradaḥ (2): One who bestows on devotees the highest wealth of all, Mokṣa.; Vāsudevaḥ: The son of Vasudeva.; Vasuḥ: He in whom all creation dwells.; Vasumānāḥ: One whose mind dwells equally in all things.; Haviḥ: Havis, the sacrificial oblation.

padas.meaning: One who, being all-pervading, is said to be endowed with speed like that of the mind.
Tīrtha means Vidyā, a branch of knowledge or skill. One who is the source of all sacred knowledge.
retāḥ – He whose Retas (creative essence) is golden (Vasu) in nature.
One who gladly bestows wealth in abundance; the true master of all wealth.
One who bestows on devotees the highest wealth of all, Mokṣa.
The son of Vasudeva.
He in whom all creation dwells.
One whose mind dwells equally in all things.
Havis, the sacrificial oblation.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सत्ता सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः ।
शूरसेनो यदुश्रेष्ठः सन्निवासः सुयामुनः ॥७५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सद्गतिः सत्कृतिः सत्ता सद्भूतिः सत्परायणः । | शूरसेनो यदुश्रेष्ठः सन्निवासः सुयामुनः ॥७५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sadgatiḥ satkṛtiḥ sattā sadbhūtiḥ satparāyaṇaḥ,
śūraseno yaduśreṣṭhaḥ sannivāsaḥ suyāmunaḥ. (75)
shlokas.meaning_english: Sadgatiḥ: One who is attained by the virtuous; or one who is endowed with intelligence of great excellence.; Satkṛtiḥ: One whose achievements are for the protection of the world.; Sattā: Experience that is without any internal or external differences – Pure Being.; Sad: bhūtiḥ – The Paramātman who is pure existence and consciousness, unsublatable and manifesting in many ways.; Satparāyaṇaḥ: He who is the highest status attainable by holy men who have realised the Truth.; Śūrasenaḥ: One having an army of heroic warriors like Hanumān.; Yaduśreṣṭhaḥ: One who is the greatest among the Yadus.; Sannivāsaḥ: One who is the resort of holy and knowing ones.; Suyāmunaḥ: One surrounded by illustrious persons associated with the river Yamunā: Devakī, Vasudeva, Nandagopa, Yaśodā, Balarāma, Subhadrā and others.

padas.meaning: One who is attained by the virtuous; or one who is endowed with intelligence of great excellence.
One whose achievements are for the protection of the world.
Experience that is without any internal or external differences – Pure Being.

He who is the highest status attainable by holy men who have realised the Truth.
One having an army of heroic warriors like Hanumān.
One who is the greatest among the Yadus.
One who is the resort of holy and knowing ones.
One surrounded by illustrious persons associated with the river Yamunā: Devakī, Vasudeva, Nandagopa, Yaśodā, Balarāma, Subhadrā and others.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भूतावासो वासुदेवः सर्वासुनिलयोऽनलः ।
दर्पहा दर्पदो दृप्तो दुर्धरोऽथापराजितः ॥७६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भूतावासो वासुदेवः सर्वासुनिलयोऽनलः । | दर्पहा दर्पदो दृप्तो दुर्धरोऽथापराजितः ॥७६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
bhūtāvāso vāsudevaḥ sarvāsunilayo 'nalaḥ,
darpahā darpado dṛpto durddharo 'thāparājitaḥ. (76)
shlokas.meaning_english: Bhūtāvāsaḥ: He in whom all beings dwell.; Vāsudevaḥ: The Divinity who pervades the whole universe by Māyā.; Sarvāsunilayaḥ: He in whose form as the Jīva all the vital energy (Prāṇa) of all living beings dissolves.; Analaḥ: One whose wealth or power has no limits.; Darpahā: One who subdues the pride of those who walk the unrighteous path.; Darpadaḥ: One who endows those who walk the path of righteousness with a sense of dignified self-respect.; Dṛptaḥ: One who is ever satisfied through the enjoyment of His own inherent bliss.; Durdharaḥ: One who is very difficult to contain in the heart during meditation.; Aparājitaḥ: One who is never conquered by internal enemies like attachment nor by external enemies like the Asuras.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
विश्वमूर्तिर्महामूर्तिर्दीप्तमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान् ।
अनेकमूर्तिरव्यक्तः शतमूर्तिः शताननः ॥७७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: विश्वमूर्तिर्महामूर्तिर्दीप्तमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान् । | अनेकमूर्तिरव्यक्तः शतमूर्तिः शताननः ॥७७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
viśvamūrtir mahāmūrtir dīptamūrtir amūrtimān,
anekamūrtir avyaktaḥ śatamūrtiḥ śatānanaḥ. (77)
shlokas.meaning_english: Viśvamūrtiḥ: One who, being the soul of all, has the whole universe as His body.; Mahāmūrtiḥ: One with an enormous form reclining on the serpent-couch of Ādiśeṣa.; Dīptamūrtiḥ: One with a luminous form of knowledge.; Amūrtimān: He who is without a body born of Karma.; Anekamūrtiḥ: One who assumes several bodies in His incarnations in order to help the world.; Avyaktaḥ: One who, though having many forms, cannot be clearly pointed to as 'This'.; Śatamūrtiḥ: One who, though of the nature of Pure Consciousness, assumes different forms for temporary purposes.; Śatānanaḥ: One with a hundred faces – indicating that He has countless forms.

padas.meaning: One who, being the soul of all, has the whole universe as His body.
One with an enormous form reclining on the serpent-couch of Ādiśeṣa.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
एको नैकः सवः कः किं यत् तत्पदमनुत्तमम् ।
लोकबन्धुर्लोकनाथो माधवो भक्तवत्सलः ॥७८॥

shlokas.iast_transliteration:
eko naikaḥ savaḥ kaḥ kiṃ yat tat padam anuttamam,
lokabandhuḥ lokānātho mādhavo bhaktavatsalaḥ. (78)
shlokas.meaning_english: Ekaḥ: One without any kind of internal, external or dissimilar differences – absolutely non-dual.; Naikaḥ: One who has numerous bodies born of Māyā.; Savaḥ: That Yajña in which Soma is prepared and used.; Kaḥ: The syllable 'Ka' indicates joy or happiness; thus one who is hymned as constituted of joy.; Kim: One who is fit to be contemplated upon, being the summation of all values.; Yat: One who is by nature self-existent; 'Yat' indicates a self- subsisting entity.; Tat: Brahma is so called because He 'expands' (Tanoti).; Padamanuttamam: Brahman is 'Pada' or the ultimate Status – the goal of all Mokṣa-seekers. It is Anuttama because there is nothing beyond It to be attained.; Lokabandhuḥ: One who is the friend of all the worlds.; Lokānāthaḥ: One to whom all the worlds pray.; Mādhavaḥ: One who was born in the clan of Madhu.; Bhaktavatsalaḥ: One who has boundless love for devotees.

padas.meaning: One without any kind of internal, external or dissimilar differences – absolutely non-dual.
One who has numerous bodies born of Māyā.
That Yajña in which Soma is prepared and used.

One who was born in the clan of Madhu.
One who has boundless love for devotees.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सुवर्णवर्णो हेमाङ्गो वराङ्गश्चन्दनाङ्गदी ।
वीरहा विषमः शून्यो घृताशीरचलश्चलः ॥७९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सुवर्णवर्णो हेमाङ्गो वराङ्गश्चन्दनाङ्गदी । | वीरहा विषमः शून्यो घृताशीरचलश्चलः ॥७९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
suvarṇavarṇo hemāṅgo varāṅgaś candanāṅgadī,

shlokas.meaning_english: Suvarṇavarṇaḥ: One who has the colour of gold.; Hemāṅgaḥ: One whose form is like gold.; Varāṅgaḥ: He whose bodily parts are all brilliantly beautiful.; Candanāṅgadī: One who is adorned with fragrant sandalwood paste and armlets that generate joy.; Vīrahā: One who destroyed heroes (Vīras) like Hiraṇyakaśipu for protecting Dharma.; Viṣamaḥ: One to whom there is no equal, because nothing is comparable to Him by any characteristic.; Śūnyaḥ: One who, being without any limiting attributes, appears as Śūnya (emptiness) to those seeking to define Him.; Ghṛtāśīḥ: One whose blessings are unfailing.; Acalaḥ: One who cannot be deprived of His real nature as Truth, Intelligence and Infinity.; Calaḥ: One who moves in the form of air (Vāyu).

One whose form is like gold.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अमानी मानदो मान्यो लोकस्वामी त्रिलोकधृक् ।
सुमेधा मेधजो धन्यः सत्यमेधा धराधरः ॥८०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अमानी मानदो मान्यो लोकस्वामी त्रिलोकधृक् । | सुमेधा मेधजो धन्यः सत्यमेधा धराधरः ॥८०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
amānī mānado mānyo lokasvāmī trilokadhṛk,
sumedhā medhajo dhanyaḥ satyamedhā dharādharaḥ. (80)
shlokas.meaning_english: Amānī: He who, being of the nature of Pure Consciousness, has no sense of identification with anything that is not the Ātman.; Mānadaḥ: One who by His Māyā induces the sense of self in non- self; or one who bestows honour and grace upon devotees.; Mānyaḥ: One who is to be adored by all, because He is the God of all.; Lokasvāmī: One who is the Lord of all the fourteen spheres.; Trilokadhṛt: One who supports all the three worlds.; Sumedhāḥ: One with great and beneficent intelligence.; Medhajaḥ: One who arose from Yāga (a kind of sacrifice).; Dhanyaḥ: One who has attained all His ends and is therefore perfectly self-satisfied.; Satyamedhāḥ: One whose intelligence always bears fruit.; Dharādharaḥ: One who supports the worlds through His fractions (aspects) like Ādiśeṣa.

padas.meaning: He who, being of the nature of Pure Consciousness, has no sense of identification with anything that is not the Ātman.

One who is the Lord of all the fourteen spheres.
One who supports all the three worlds.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
तेजोवृषो द्युतिधरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः ।
प्रग्रहो निग्रहो व्यग्रो नैकशृङ्गो गदाग्रजः ॥८१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: तेजोवृषो द्युतिधरः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः । | प्रग्रहो निग्रहो व्यग्रो नैकशृङ्गो गदाग्रजः ॥८१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
tejovṛṣo dyutidharaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ,
pragraho nigraho vyagro naikaśṛṅgo gadāgrajaḥ. (81)
shlokas.meaning_english: Tejovṛṣaḥ: One who in the form of the sun causes rainfall at all times.; Dyutidharaḥ: One whose form is always resplendent.; Sarva: śastra-bhṛtāṃ varaḥ – One who is superior to all who bear arms.; Pragrahaḥ: One who accepts the offerings of devotees with great delight.; Nigrahaḥ: One who controls and ultimately dissolves everything.; Vyagraḥ: One who has no end (Agra). Or one who is the elder brother of Gada.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
चतुर्मूर्तिश्चतुर्बाहुश्चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्गतिः ।
चतुरात्मा चतुर्भावश्चतुर्वेदविदेकपात् ॥८२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: चतुर्मूर्तिश्चतुर्बाहुश्चतुर्व्यूहश्चतुर्गतिः । | चतुरात्मा चतुर्भावश्चतुर्वेदविदेकपात् ॥८२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
caturmūrtiś caturbāhuś caturvyūhaś caturgatiḥ,
caturātmā caturbhāvaś caturvedavid ekapāt. (82)
shlokas.meaning_english: Caturmūrtiḥ: One with four aspects: Virāṭ, Sūtrātman, Avyākṛta and Turīya. shlokas.full_sanskrit:
समावर्तोऽनिवृत्तात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः ।
दुर्लभो दुर्गमो दुर्गो दुरावासो दुरारिहा ॥८३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: समावर्तोऽनिवृत्तात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः । | दुर्लभो दुर्गमो दुर्गो दुरावासो दुरारिहा ॥८३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
samāvarto 'nivṛttātmā durjayo duratikramaḥ,
durlabho durgamo durgo durāvāso durārihā. (83)
shlokas.meaning_english: Samāvartaḥ: One who effectively whirls the wheel of Saṃsāra.; Anivṛttātmā: One who is not separated from anything or anywhere, because He is all-pervading.; Durjayaḥ: One who cannot be conquered.; Duratikramaḥ: One out of fear of whom even heavenly beings like the sun dare not oppose His command.; Durlabhaḥ: One who can be attained by Bhakti, which is itself difficult to cultivate.; Durgamaḥ: One whom it is difficult to attain.; Durgaḥ: One the attainment of whom is rendered difficult by various obstacles.; Durāvāsaḥ: He whom Yogīs, only with great difficulty, bring to reside in their hearts in Samādhi.; Durārihā: One who destroys inimical beings like the Asuras.

One who cannot be conquered.
One out of fear of whom even heavenly beings like the sun dare not oppose His command.
One who can be attained by Bhakti, which is itself difficult to cultivate.
One whom it is difficult to attain.
One the attainment of whom is rendered difficult by various obstacles.
He whom Yogīs, only with great difficulty, bring to reside in their hearts in Samādhi.
One who destroys inimical beings like the Asuras.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
शुभाङ्गो लोकसारङ्गः सुतन्तुस्तन्तुवर्धनः ।
इन्द्रकर्मा महाकर्मा कृतकर्मा कृतागमः ॥८४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: शुभाङ्गो लोकसारङ्गः सुतन्तुस्तन्तुवर्धनः । | इन्द्रकर्मा महाकर्मा कृतकर्मा कृतागमः ॥८४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śubhāṅgo lokasāraṅgaḥ sutantus tantuvardhanaḥ,
indrakarmā mahākarmā kṛtakarmā kṛtāgamaḥ. (84)
shlokas.meaning_english: Śubhāṅgaḥ: One whose form is very auspicious to meditate upon.; Lokasāraṅgaḥ: One who like the Sāraṅga (honey-bee) extracts the essence from the world.; Sutantuḥ: As this universe of infinite extension belongs to Him, the Lord is called Sutantu ('beautiful web').; Tantu: vardhanaḥ – One who can augment or contract the web of this world.; Indra: karmā – One whose actions are like those of Indra – highly commendable and excellent.; Mahākarmā: One of whom the great elements like Ākāśa are effects.; Kṛtakarmā: One who has fulfilled everything and has nothing more to accomplish.; Kṛtāgamaḥ: One who has given out the Āgama in the form of the Veda.

padas.meaning: One whose form is very auspicious to meditate upon.
One who like the Sāraṅga (honey-bee) extracts the essence from the world.
As this universe of infinite extension belongs to Him, the Lord is called Sutantu ('beautiful web').
vardhanaḥ – One who can augment or contract the web of this world.
karmā – One whose actions are like those of Indra – highly commendable and excellent.
One of whom the great elements like Ākāśa are effects.
One who has fulfilled everything and has nothing more to accomplish.
One who has given out the Āgama in the form of the Veda.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दो रत्ननाभः सुलोचनः ।
अर्को वाजसनः शृङ्गी जयन्तः सर्वविज्जयी ॥८५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: उद्भवः सुन्दरः सुन्दो रत्ननाभः सुलोचनः । | अर्को वाजसनः शृङ्गी जयन्तः सर्वविज्जयी ॥८५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
udbhavaḥ sundaraḥ sundo ratnanābhaḥ sulocanaḥ,
arko vājasanaḥ śṛṅgī jayantaḥ sarvavij jayī. (85)
shlokas.meaning_english: Udbhavaḥ: One who assumes great and noble embodiments entirely out of His own will.; Sundaraḥ: One who has a graceful beauty that enchants everyone.; Sundaḥ: One noted for extreme tenderness (Undana).; Ratna: nābhaḥ – Ratna indicates beauty; one whose navel is exceedingly beautiful.; Sulocanaḥ: One who has brilliant eyes, the knowledge of everything.; Arkaḥ: One who is worshipped even by beings like Brahmā who are themselves objects of worship.; Vājasanaḥ: One who gives Vāja (food) to those who entreat Him.; Śṛṅgī: One who at the time of Pralaya assumed the form of a fish with a prominent horn.; Jayantaḥ: One who conquers enemies easily.; Sarvavijjayī: The Lord is 'Sarvavit' (all-knowing) and 'Jayī' (conqueror of all inner forces like attachment and anger as well as outer foes like Hiraṇyākṣa).

padas.meaning: One who assumes great and noble embodiments entirely out of His own will.
One who has a graceful beauty that enchants everyone.
One noted for extreme tenderness (Undana).
nābhaḥ – Ratna indicates beauty; one whose navel is exceedingly beautiful.
One who has brilliant eyes, the knowledge of everything.
One who is worshipped even by beings like Brahmā who are themselves objects of worship.
One who gives Vāja (food) to those who entreat Him.
One who at the time of Pralaya assumed the form of a fish with a prominent horn.
One who conquers enemies easily.
The Lord is 'Sarvavit' (all-knowing) and 'Jayī' (conqueror of all inner forces like attachment and anger as well as outer foes like Hiraṇyākṣa).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सुवर्णबिन्दुरक्षोभ्यः सर्ववागीश्वरेश्वरः ।
महाह्रदो महागर्तो महाभूतो महानिधिः ॥८६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सुवर्णबिन्दुरक्षोभ्यः सर्ववागीश्वरेश्वरः । | महाह्रदो महागर्तो महाभूतो महानिधिः ॥८६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
suvarṇabindur akṣobhyaḥ sarvavāgīśvareśvaraḥ,
mahāhrado mahāgarto mahābhūto mahānidhiḥ. (86)
shlokas.meaning_english: Suvarṇabinduḥ: One whose limbs (Bindus) are equal to gold in brilliance.; Akṣobhyaḥ: One who is never perturbed by passions like attachment and aversion, by sense-objects, nor by the Asuras.; Sarva: vāgīśvareśvaraḥ – One who is the master of all masters of learning, including Brahmā.; Mahāhradaḥ: He is called a great lake (Hrada) because, being the Paramātman of the nature of Bliss, Yogīs who contemplate on Him dip themselves in that lake of Bliss and attain great joy.; Mahāgartaḥ: One whose Māyā is as difficult to cross as a great pit.; Mahābhūtaḥ: One who is undivided by the three periods of time – past, present and future.; Mahānidhiḥ: One in whom all the great elements have their support – the Mahān (great) and most precious (Nidhi).

padas.meaning: One whose limbs (Bindus) are equal to gold in brilliance.
One who is never perturbed by passions like attachment and aversion, by sense-objects, nor by the Asuras.
vāgīśvareśvaraḥ – One who is the master of all masters of learning, including Brahmā.
He is called a great lake (Hrada) because, being the Paramātman of the nature of Bliss, Yogīs who contemplate on Him dip themselves in that lake of Bliss and attain great joy.
One whose Māyā is as difficult to cross as a great pit.
One who is undivided by the three periods of time – past, present and future.
One in whom all the great elements have their support – the Mahān (great) and most precious (Nidhi).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनोऽनिलः ।
अमृताशोऽमृतवपुः सर्वज्ञः सर्वतोमुखः ॥८७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: कुमुदः कुन्दरः कुन्दः पर्जन्यः पावनोऽनिलः । | अमृताशोऽमृतवपुः सर्वज्ञः सर्वतोमुखः ॥८७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
kumudaḥ kundaraḥ kundaḥ parjanyaḥ pāvano 'nilaḥ,
amṛtāśo 'mṛtavapuḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ. (87)
shlokas.meaning_english: Kumudaḥ: 'Ku' means earth; one who gives joy (muda) to the earth by freeing it of its burdens.; Kundaraḥ: One who offers blessings as pure as the Kunda (jasmine) flower.; Kundaḥ: One whose limbs are as beautiful as the Kunda (jasmine).; Parjanyaḥ: One who, like a cloud, extinguishes the three Tāpas (miseries) – from psychological, material and spiritual causes – and rains down all desired things.; Pāvanaḥ: One by merely remembering whom a devotee attains purity.; Anilaḥ: One who is without any inducement or conditioning; also 'one who never sleeps', ever awake.; Amṛtāśaḥ: One who consumes Amṛta (immortal bliss), which is His own nature.; Amṛtavapuḥ: One whose form is deathless and undecaying.; Sarvajñaḥ: One who is all-knowing.; Sarvatomukhaḥ: One who has faces everywhere.

padas.meaning: 'Ku' means earth; one who gives joy (muda) to the earth by freeing it of its burdens.
One who offers blessings as pure as the Kunda (jasmine) flower.
One whose limbs are as beautiful as the Kunda (jasmine).
One who, like a cloud, extinguishes the three Tāpas (miseries) – from psychological, material and spiritual causes – and rains down all desired things.
One by merely remembering whom a devotee attains purity.
One who is without any inducement or conditioning; also 'one who never sleeps', ever awake.
One who consumes Amṛta (immortal bliss), which is His own nature.
One whose form is deathless and undecaying.
One who is all-knowing.
One who has faces everywhere.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सुलभः सुव्रतः सिद्धः शत्रुजिच्छत्रुतापनः ।
न्यग्रोधोऽदुम्बरोऽश्वत्थश्चाणूरान्ध्रनिषूदनः ॥८८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सुलभः सुव्रतः सिद्धः शत्रुजिच्छत्रुतापनः । | न्यग्रोधोऽदुम्बरोऽश्वत्थश्चाणूरान्ध्रनिषूदनः ॥८८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sulabhaḥ suvrataḥ siddhaḥ śatrujic chatrutāpanaḥ,
nyagrodho 'dumbaro 'śvatthaś cāṇūrāndhraniṣūdanaḥ. (88)
shlokas.meaning_english: Sulabhaḥ: One who is attained easily by offering trifles – leaf, flower and fruit – with devotion.; Suvrataḥ: One who enjoys pure offerings; or one who is a mere witness (non-enjoyer).; Siddhaḥ: One whose purposes are always accomplished – omnipotent and unobstructed by any other will.; Śatrujit: Conqueror of all forces of evil.; Śatrutāpanaḥ: One who destroys the enemies of the Devas.; Nyagrodhaḥ: That which remains above all and yet grows downward – the source of all that is manifest.; Udumbaraḥ: One who, as the Supreme cause, is 'above the sky' – superior to all.; Aśvatthaḥ: That which does not last even until the next day – the ever-changing universe as His form.; Cāṇūrāndhra: niṣūdanaḥ – One who destroyed the valiant fighter Cāṇūra belonging to the Āndhra race.

padas.meaning: One who is attained easily by offering trifles – leaf, flower and fruit – with devotion.
One who enjoys pure offerings; or one who is a mere witness (non-enjoyer).
One whose purposes are always accomplished – omnipotent and unobstructed by any other will.
Conqueror of all forces of evil.
One who destroys the enemies of the Devas.
That which remains above all and yet grows downward – the source of all that is manifest.
One who, as the Supreme cause, is 'above the sky' – superior to all.
That which does not last even until the next day – the ever-changing universe as His form.
niṣūdanaḥ – One who destroyed the valiant fighter Cāṇūra belonging to the Āndhra race.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सहस्रार्चिः सप्तजिह्वः सप्तैधाः सप्तवाहनः ।
अमूर्तिरनघोऽचिन्त्यो भयकृद्भयनाशनः ॥८९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सहस्रार्चिः सप्तजिह्वः सप्तैधाः सप्तवाहनः । | अमूर्तिरनघोऽचिन्त्यो भयकृद्भयनाशनः ॥८९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sahasrārciḥ saptajihvaḥ saptaidhāḥ saptavāhanaḥ,
amūrtir anagho 'cintyo bhayakṛd bhayanāśanaḥ. (89)
shlokas.meaning_english: Sahasrārciḥ: One with innumerable rays (Arcis).; Sapta: jihvaḥ – The Lord in His manifestation as Fire is conceived as having seven tongues of flame.; Saptaidhāḥ: The Lord who is of the nature of fire has seven Edhās (forms of brilliance).; Saptavāhanaḥ: The Lord in the form of Sūrya (sun) has seven horses as His vehicles.; Amūrtiḥ: One who is without a gross physical form, formless pure consciousness.; Anaghaḥ: One who is without sin or sorrow.; Acintyaḥ: One who is not determinable by any criteria of knowledge, being Himself the witnessing Self certifying all knowledge.; Bhayakṛt: One who generates fear in those who walk the evil path; or one who cuts at the root of all fear.; Bhaya: nāśanaḥ – One who destroys the fears of the virtuous.

One who is without sin or sorrow.
One who is not determinable by any criteria of knowledge, being Himself the witnessing Self certifying all knowledge.
One who generates fear in those who walk the evil path; or one who cuts at the root of all fear.
nāśanaḥ – One who destroys the fears of the virtuous.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अणुर्बृहत्कृशः स्थूलो गुणभृन्निर्गुणो महान् ।
अधृतः स्वधृतः स्वास्यः प्राग्वंशो वंशवर्धनः ॥९०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अणुर्बृहत्कृशः स्थूलो गुणभृन्निर्गुणो महान् । | अधृतः स्वधृतः स्वास्यः प्राग्वंशो वंशवर्धनः ॥९०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
aṇur bṛhat kṛśaḥ sthūlo guṇabhṛn nirguṇo mahān,

shlokas.meaning_english: Aṇuḥ: One who is extremely subtle.; Bṛhat: The huge and mighty.; Kṛśaḥ: One who is non-material; beyond all Prakṛtic substance.; Sthūlaḥ: Being the inner pervader of all, He is described as Sthūla (huge) in a figurative sense.; Guṇa: bhṛt – The support of the Guṇas – Sattva, Rajas and Tamas – through which creation, sustentation and dissolution are performed.; Nirguṇaḥ: One who is without the Guṇas of Prakṛti.; Mahān: The great.; Adhṛtaḥ: One who, being the support of all supporting agencies like Pṛthvī (Earth), is Himself not supported by anything external.; Svadhṛtaḥ: One supported only by Himself.; Svāsyaḥ: One whose face is beautiful and slightly red, like the inside of a lotus flower.; Prāgvaṃśaḥ: The Lord's 'lineage' (the world-system) is not preceded by any prior cause – He alone is the ultimate.; Vaṃśavardhanaḥ: One who augments or dissolves the world- system, which is His offspring.

One who is without the Guṇas of Prakṛti.
The great.
One who, being the support of all supporting agencies like Pṛthvī (Earth), is Himself not supported by anything external.
One supported only by Himself.
One whose face is beautiful and slightly red, like the inside of a lotus flower.
The Lord's 'lineage' (the world-system) is not preceded by any prior cause – He alone is the ultimate.
One who augments or dissolves the world- system, which is His offspring.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भारभृत् कथितो योगी योगीशः सर्वकामदः ।
आश्रमः श्रमणः क्षामः सुपर्णो वायुवाहनः ॥९१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भारभृत् कथितो योगी योगीशः सर्वकामदः । | आश्रमः श्रमणः क्षामः सुपर्णो वायुवाहनः ॥९१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
bhārabhṛt kathito yogī yogīśaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ,
āśramaḥ śramaṇaḥ kṣāmaḥ suparṇo vāyuvāhanaḥ. (91)
shlokas.meaning_english: Bhārabhṛt: One who bears the weight of the earth by assuming the form of Ananta (Ādiśeṣa).; Kathitaḥ: One who is spoken of as the highest by the Veda, of whom all Vedas speak.; Yogī: Yoga here means knowledge; He who is attained by that is Yogī. Or one ever established in His own Self, the Paramātmā.; Yogīśaḥ: He who is never shaken from Yoga or knowledge of the Self, unlike ordinary Yogīs who slip away on account of obstacles.; Sarva: kāmadaḥ – One who bestows all desired fruits.; Āśramaḥ: One who is the bestower of rest on all who are wandering in the forest of Saṃsāra.; Śramaṇaḥ: One who brings tribulations to those who live without using their discriminative wisdom.; Kṣāmaḥ: He who brings about the decline and dissolution of all beings.; Suparṇaḥ: The Lord manifested as the tree of Saṃsāra has excellent leaves (Parṇa) in the form of Vedic passages (Chandas).; Vāyuvāhanaḥ: He for fear of whom Vāyu (Air) carries all beings.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
धनुर्धरो धनुर्वेदो दण्डो दमयिता दमः ।
अपराजितः सर्वसहो नियन्ताऽनियमोऽयमः ॥९२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: धनुर्धरो धनुर्वेदो दण्डो दमयिता दमः । | अपराजितः सर्वसहो नियन्ताऽनियमोऽयमः ॥९२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
dhanurdharo dhanurvedo daṇḍo damayitā damaḥ,
aparājitaḥ sarvasaho niyantā 'niyamo 'yamaḥ. (92)
shlokas.meaning_english: Dhanurdharaḥ: He who, as Rāma, wielded the great bow.; Dhanurvedaḥ: He who, as Rāma the son of Daśaratha, was master of the science of archery (Dhanurveda).; Daṇḍaḥ: He who is discipline personified among all disciplinarians.; Damayitā: He who inflicts punishment on the wicked as Yama and as king.; Damaḥ: He who is self-discipline in men as a result of righteous enforcement.; Aparājitaḥ: One who is never defeated by any enemy.; Sarvasahaḥ: One who is expert in all Karmas (works) and bears all with equanimity.; Niyantā: One who appoints every person to their respective duties.; Aniyamaḥ: One upon whom no external law is enforced, being Himself the controller of everything.; Ayamaḥ: One upon whom Yama has no control; one who has no death.

He who is discipline personified among all disciplinarians.
He who inflicts punishment on the wicked as Yama and as king.
He who is self-discipline in men as a result of righteous enforcement.
One who is never defeated by any enemy.
One who is expert in all Karmas (works) and bears all with equanimity.
One who appoints every person to their respective duties.
One upon whom no external law is enforced, being Himself the controller of everything.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सत्त्ववान् सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्यधर्मपरायणः ।
अभिप्रायः प्रियार्होऽर्हः प्रियकृत् प्रीतिवर्धनः ॥९३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सत्त्ववान् सात्त्विकः सत्यः सत्यधर्मपरायणः । | अभिप्रायः प्रियार्होऽर्हः प्रियकृत् प्रीतिवर्धनः ॥९३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sattvavān sāttvikaḥ satyaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ,
abhiprāyaḥ priyārho 'rhaḥ priyakṛt prītivardhanāḥ. (93)
shlokas.meaning_english: Sattvavān: One who has the strengthening qualities: heroism, prowess, fortitude, etc.; Sāttvikaḥ: One essentially established in the Sattva Guṇa.; Satyaḥ: One who is truly present in and established in good people.; Satya: dharma-parāyaṇaḥ – One who is the very foundation of truthfulness and righteousness in all their aspects.; Abhiprāyaḥ: The One sought after by those who seek the ultimate values of life (Puruṣārtha).; Priyārhaḥ: The being to whom whatever is dearest to oneself is fittingly offered.; Arhaḥ: One who deserves to be worshipped with all the ingredients and rites of worship.; Priyakṛt: One who not only merits love but who actively does what is good and dear to those who worship Him.; Prītivardhanāḥ: One who enhances the joy and devotion of His devotees.
