The One sought after by those who seek the ultimate values of life (Puruṣārtha).
The being to whom whatever is dearest to oneself is fittingly offered.
One who deserves to be worshipped with all the ingredients and rites of worship.
One who not only merits love but who actively does what is good and dear to those who worship Him.
One who enhances the joy and devotion of His devotees.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
विहायसगतिर्ज्योतिः सुरुचिर्हुतभुग्विभुः ।
रविर्विरोचनः सूर्यः सविता रविलोचनः ॥९४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: विहायसगतिर्ज्योतिः सुरुचिर्हुतभुग्विभुः । | रविर्विरोचनः सूर्यः सविता रविलोचनः ॥९४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vihāyasagatir jyotiḥ surucir hutabhug vibhuḥ,
ravir virocanaḥ sūryaḥ savitā ravilocanaḥ. (94)
shlokas.meaning_english: Vihāyasa: gatiḥ – One who moves in (or is the support of) Viṣṇupada – the highest region.; Jyotiḥ: One who is the light of self-luminous consciousness that reveals itself and all other things.; Suruciḥ: The Lord whose Ruci (brilliance or will) is of an eminently attractive nature.; Hutabhuk: One who receives whatever is offered to any deity in all sacrifices.; Vibhuḥ: One who dwells everywhere; or one who is the master of all the three worlds.; Raviḥ: One who absorbs all Rasas (fluids) in the form of the Sun.; Virocanaḥ: One who shines in many ways.; Sūryaḥ: One who generates Śrī (brilliance) in Sūrya. Or Agni (Fire) is what is called Sūrya.; Savitā: One who brings forth (Prasava) all the worlds.; Ravi: locanaḥ – One having the sun as His eye.

padas.meaning: gatiḥ – One who moves in (or is the support of) Viṣṇupada – the highest region.
One who is the light of self-luminous consciousness that reveals itself and all other things.
The Lord whose Ruci (brilliance or will) is of an eminently attractive nature.
One who receives whatever is offered to any deity in all sacrifices.
One who dwells everywhere; or one who is the master of all the three worlds.
One who absorbs all Rasas (fluids) in the form of the Sun.
One who shines in many ways.
One who generates Śrī (brilliance) in Sūrya. Or Agni (Fire) is what is called Sūrya.
One who brings forth (Prasava) all the worlds.
locanaḥ – One having the sun as His eye.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अनन्तो हुतभुग्भोक्ता सुखदो नैकजोऽग्रजः ।
अनिर्विण्णः सदामर्षी लोकाधिष्ठाानमद्भुतः ॥९५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अनन्तो हुतभुग्भोक्ता सुखदो नैकजोऽग्रजः । | अनिर्विण्णः सदामर्षी लोकाधिष्ठाानमद्भुतः ॥९५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ananto hutabhug bhoktā sukhado naikajo 'grajaḥ,
anirviṇṇaḥ sadāmarṣī lokādhiṣṭhānam adbhutaḥ. (95)
shlokas.meaning_english: Anantaḥ: One who is eternal, all-pervading and indeterminable by space and time.; Hutabhuk: One who consumes what is offered in fire sacrifices.; Bhoktā: One to whom the insentient Prakṛti is the object of experience.; Sukhadaḥ: One who bestows liberation (Mokṣa) on devotees.; Naikajaḥ: One who takes birth again and again for the preservation of Dharma.; Agrajaḥ: One who was born before everything else – Hiraṇyagarbha.; Anirviṇṇaḥ: One who is free from all sorrow, having secured all His desires without any obstruction.; Sadāmarṣī: One who is always patient and forbearing towards good men.; Lokādhiṣṭhānam: Brahman who, though without any support for Himself, supports all the three worlds.; Adbhutaḥ: The wonderful, marvellous Being.

padas.meaning: One who is eternal, all-pervading and indeterminable by space and time.
One who consumes what is offered in fire sacrifices.
One to whom the insentient Prakṛti is the object of experience.
One who bestows liberation (Mokṣa) on devotees.
One who takes birth again and again for the preservation of Dharma.
One who was born before everything else – Hiraṇyagarbha.
One who is free from all sorrow, having secured all His desires without any obstruction.
One who is always patient and forbearing towards good men.
Brahman who, though without any support for Himself, supports all the three worlds.
The wonderful, marvellous Being.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सनात्सनातनतमः कपिलः कपिरव्ययः ।
स्वस्तिदः स्वस्तिकृत्स्वस्ति स्वस्तिभुक्स्वस्तिदक्षिणः ॥९६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सनात्सनातनतमः कपिलः कपिरव्ययः । | स्वस्तिदः स्वस्तिकृत्स्वस्ति स्वस्तिभुक्स्वस्तिदक्षिणः ॥९६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sanāt sanātanatamaḥ kapilaḥ kapir avyayaḥ,
svastidaḥ svastikṛt svasti svastibhuk svastidakṣiṇaḥ. (96)
shlokas.meaning_english: Sanāt: The word Sanāt indicates a great length of time; time itself is a manifestation of the Supreme Being.; Sanātanatamaḥ: Being the cause of all, He is more ancient than Brahmā and other beings who are generally considered eternal.; Kapilaḥ: A subterranean fire in the ocean, Kapila, light red in colour; also the name of the sage who embodied divine knowledge.; Kapiḥ: 'Ka' means water; one who drinks or absorbs all water by means of His form as the Sun.; Avyayaḥ: One in whom all the worlds dissolve at Pralaya without loss.; Svastidaḥ: One who gives what is auspicious to devotees.; Svastikṛt: One who works for the bestowal of what is good.; Svasti: One whose auspicious form is characterised by supreme Bliss.; Svastibhuk: One who enjoys the Svasti (auspiciousness) above, or who preserves the well-being of devotees.; Svastidakṣiṇaḥ: One who augments auspiciousness (Svasti) through His grace.

padas.meaning: The word Sanāt indicates a great length of time; time itself is a manifestation of the Supreme Being.
Being the cause of all, He is more ancient than Brahmā and other beings who are generally considered eternal.
A subterranean fire in the ocean, Kapila, light red in colour; also the name of the sage who embodied divine knowledge.
'Ka' means water; one who drinks or absorbs all water by means of His form as the Sun.
One in whom all the worlds dissolve at Pralaya without loss.
One who gives what is auspicious to devotees.
One who works for the bestowal of what is good.
One whose auspicious form is characterised by supreme Bliss.
One who enjoys the Svasti (auspiciousness) above, or who preserves the well-being of devotees.
One who augments auspiciousness (Svasti) through His grace.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अरौद्रः कुण्डली चक्री विक्रम्यूर्जितशासनः ।
शब्दातिगः शब्दसहः शिशिरः शर्वरीकरः ॥९७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अरौद्रः कुण्डली चक्री विक्रम्यूर्जितशासनः । | शब्दातिगः शब्दसहः शिशिरः शर्वरीकरः ॥९७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
araudraḥ kuṇḍalī cakrī vikramī ūrjitaśāsanaḥ,
śabdātigaḥ śabdasahaḥ śiśiraḥ śarvarīkaraḥ. (97)
shlokas.meaning_english: Araudraḥ: Action, attachment and anger are Raudra. The Lord, having all desires fulfilled, is free from attachment and anger – hence Araudra.; Kuṇḍalī: One who has taken the form of Ādiśeṣa – the coiled one.; Cakrī: One who wields the discus Sudarśana – representing Manas – for the protection of all the worlds.; Vikramī: Vikrama means taking a stride, as also great courage and valour.; Ūrjita: śāsanaḥ – One whose dictates in the form of Śrutis and Smṛtis are of an extremely sublime nature.; Śabdātigaḥ: One who cannot be denoted by any sound because He has none of the characteristics that could be grasped by words.; Śabdasahaḥ: One who is the ultimate purport of all the Vedas.; Śiśiraḥ: One who is a cooling shelter to those burning in the three types of worldly fires: sufferings from material, psychological and spiritual causes.; Śarvarīkaraḥ: For those in bondage the Ātman appears like night (Śarvarī); for the enlightened, Saṃsāra is like night. The Lord generates this 'night' of transcendence for both.

padas.meaning: Action, attachment and anger are Raudra. The Lord, having all desires fulfilled, is free from attachment and anger – hence Araudra.
One who has taken the form of Ādiśeṣa – the coiled one.
One who wields the discus Sudarśana – representing Manas – for the protection of all the worlds.
Vikrama means taking a stride, as also great courage and valour.
śāsanaḥ – One whose dictates in the form of Śrutis and Smṛtis are of an extremely sublime nature.
One who cannot be denoted by any sound because He has none of the characteristics that could be grasped by words.
One who is the ultimate purport of all the Vedas.
One who is a cooling shelter to those burning in the three types of worldly fires: sufferings from material, psychological and spiritual causes.
For those in bondage the Ātman appears like night (Śarvarī); for the enlightened, Saṃsāra is like night. The Lord generates this 'night' of transcendence for both.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अक्रूरः पेशलो दक्षो दक्षिणः क्षमिणांवरः ।
विद्वत्तमो वीतभयः पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः ॥९८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अक्रूरः पेशलो दक्षो दक्षिणः क्षमिणांवरः । | विद्वत्तमो वीतभयः पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः ॥९८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
akrūraḥ peśalo dakṣo dakṣiṇaḥ kṣamiṇāṃ varaḥ,
vidvattamo vītabhayaḥ puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanaḥ. (98)
shlokas.meaning_english: Akrūraḥ: One who is without cruelty.; Peśalaḥ: One who is handsome and graceful in action, mind, word and body.; Dakṣaḥ: One who is full-grown, strong and does everything effectively; a highly capable one.; Dakṣiṇaḥ: One who is expert and adroit; same purport as the above name from another angle.; Kṣamiṇāṃ varaḥ: The greatest among the patient ones, more patient than all Yogīs noted for forbearance.; Vidvattamaḥ: He who possesses unsurpassable and all-inclusive knowledge of everything.; Vītabhayaḥ: One who, being eternally free and Lord of all, is free from any fear of transmigratory life.; Puṇya: śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ – One to hear about and to sing of whom is deeply meritorious.

padas.meaning: One who is without cruelty.
One who is handsome and graceful in action, mind, word and body.
One who is full-grown, strong and does everything effectively; a highly capable one.
One who is expert and adroit; same purport as the above name from another angle.
The greatest among the patient ones, more patient than all Yogīs noted for forbearance.
He who possesses unsurpassable and all-inclusive knowledge of everything.
One who, being eternally free and Lord of all, is free from any fear of transmigratory life.
śravaṇa-kīrtanaḥ – One to hear about and to sing of whom is deeply meritorious.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
उत्तारणो दुष्कृतिहा पुण्यो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः ।
वीरहा रक्षणः सन्तो जीवनः पर्यवस्थितः ॥९९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: उत्तारणो दुष्कृतिहा पुण्यो दुःस्वप्ननाशनः । | वीरहा रक्षणः सन्तो जीवनः पर्यवस्थितः ॥९९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
uttāraṇo duṣkṛtihā puṇyo duḥsvapnanāśanaḥ,
vīrahā rakṣaṇaḥ santo jīvanaḥ paryavasthitaḥ. (99)
shlokas.meaning_english: Uttāraṇaḥ: One who takes beings across to the other shore of the ocean of Saṃsāra.; Duṣkṛtihā: One who effaces the evil effects of evil actions; or one who destroys those who perform evil.; Puṇyaḥ: One who bestows holiness on those who remember and adore Him.; Duḥsvapna: nāśanaḥ – When adored and meditated upon, He saves one from dreams foreboding danger.; Vīrahā: One who frees Jīvas from bondage, saving them from transmigratory paths by bestowing liberation.; Rakṣaṇaḥ: One who, endowed with Sattvaguṇa, protects all the three worlds.; Santaḥ: Those who adopt the virtuous path are called Santas (good people); the Lord is their very soul.; Jīvanaḥ: One who sustains the lives of all beings as Prāṇa.; Paryavasthitaḥ: One who remains pervading everywhere in this universe.

padas.meaning: One who takes beings across to the other shore of the ocean of Saṃsāra.
One who effaces the evil effects of evil actions; or one who destroys those who perform evil.
One who bestows holiness on those who remember and adore Him.
nāśanaḥ – When adored and meditated upon, He saves one from dreams foreboding danger.
One who frees Jīvas from bondage, saving them from transmigratory paths by bestowing liberation.
One who, endowed with Sattvaguṇa, protects all the three worlds.
Those who adopt the virtuous path are called Santas (good people); the Lord is their very soul.
One who sustains the lives of all beings as Prāṇa.
One who remains pervading everywhere in this universe.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अनन्तरूपोऽनन्तश्रीर्जितमन्युर्भयापहः ।
चतुरश्रो गभीरात्मा विदिशो व्यादिशो दिशः ॥१००॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अनन्तरूपोऽनन्तश्रीर्जितमन्युर्भयापहः । | चतुरश्रो गभीरात्मा विदिशो व्यादिशो दिशः ॥१००॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
anantarūpo 'nantaśrīr jitamanyur bhayāpahaḥ,
caturaśro gabhīrātmā vidiśo vyādiśo diśaḥ. (100)
shlokas.meaning_english: Ananta: rūpaḥ – One who has innumerable forms, as He dwells in this all-comprehending universe.; Anantaśrīḥ: One whose Śrī (glory) is infinite.; Jita: manyuḥ – One who has overcome anger.; Bhayāpahaḥ: One who destroys the fears of beings arising from Saṃsāra.; Caturaśraḥ: One who is just, bestowing on Jīvas the fruits of their Karma.; Gabhīrātmā: One whose nature is unfathomable.; Vidiśaḥ: One who distributes various fruits of actions to persons differing in form according to their competency.; Vyādiśaḥ: One who gives to Indra and other deities directions according to their varied functions.; Diśaḥ: One who in the form of the Vedas bestows the fruits of ritualistic actions on different beings.

padas.meaning: rūpaḥ – One who has innumerable forms, as He dwells in this all-comprehending universe.
One whose Śrī (glory) is infinite.
manyuḥ – One who has overcome anger.
One who destroys the fears of beings arising from Saṃsāra.
One who is just, bestowing on Jīvas the fruits of their Karma.
One whose nature is unfathomable.
One who distributes various fruits of actions to persons differing in form according to their competency.
One who gives to Indra and other deities directions according to their varied functions.
One who in the form of the Vedas bestows the fruits of ritualistic actions on different beings.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अनादिर्भूर्भुवो लक्ष्मीः सुवीरो रुचिराङ्गदः ।
जननो जनजन्मादिर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः ॥१०१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अनादिर्भूर्भुवो लक्ष्मीः सुवीरो रुचिराङ्गदः । | जननो जनजन्मादिर्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः ॥१०१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
anādir bhūrbhuvo lakṣmīḥ suvīro rucirāṅgadaḥ,
janano janajanmādir bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ. (101)
shlokas.meaning_english: Anādiḥ: One who has no beginning, being the ultimate cause of all.; Bhūrbhuvaḥ: 'Bhu' means support; one who is the support of even the earth, which itself supports all things.; Lakṣmīḥ: He who is the bestower of all that is auspicious to the earth, besides being its supporter.; Suvīraḥ: One who has many brilliant ways of manifestation.; Rucirāṅgadaḥ: One who wears very attractive armlets.; Jananaḥ: One who gives birth to all living beings.; Jana: janmādiḥ – One who is the root cause of the origin of Jīvas that come to have embodiment.; Bhīmaḥ: One who is the cause of awe and fear.; Bhīma: parākramaḥ – One whose power and courage in His incarnations was a cause of terror for the Asuras.

padas.meaning: One who has no beginning, being the ultimate cause of all.
'Bhu' means support; one who is the support of even the earth, which itself supports all things.
He who is the bestower of all that is auspicious to the earth, besides being its supporter.
One who has many brilliant ways of manifestation.
One who wears very attractive armlets.
One who gives birth to all living beings.
janmādiḥ – One who is the root cause of the origin of Jīvas that come to have embodiment.
One who is the cause of awe and fear.
parākramaḥ – One whose power and courage in His incarnations was a cause of terror for the Asuras.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
आधारनिलयोऽधाता पुष्पहासः प्रजागरः ।
ऊर्ध्वगः सत्पथाचारः प्राणदः प्रणवः पणः ॥१०२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: आधारनिलयोऽधाता पुष्पहासः प्रजागरः । | ऊर्ध्वगः सत्पथाचारः प्राणदः प्रणवः पणः ॥१०२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ādhāranilayo 'dhātā puṣpahāsaḥ prajāgaraḥ,
ūrdhvagaḥ satpathācāraḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ paṇaḥ. (102)
shlokas.meaning_english: Ādhāra: nilayaḥ – One who is the support of all basic supporting factors – the five elements (Ether, Air, Fire, Water and Earth).; Adhātā: One who is His own support and therefore requires no external support.; Puṣpahāsaḥ: One whose manifestation as the universe resembles the blooming (Hāsa) of buds into flowers.; Prajāgaraḥ: One who is particularly awake – being eternal Awareness itself.; Ūrdhvagaḥ: One who is above everything.; Satpathācāraḥ: One who always follows the conduct of the good.; Prāṇadaḥ: One who restores life to the dead, as in the case of Parīkṣit.; Praṇavaḥ: Praṇava (Oṃ) – the manifesting sound-symbol of Brahman. As He is inseparably related to Praṇava, He is called Praṇava.; Paṇaḥ: From the root meaning transaction – one who bestows the fruits of Karma on all according to their actions.

padas.meaning: nilayaḥ – One who is the support of all basic supporting factors – the five elements (Ether, Air, Fire, Water and Earth).
One who is His own support and therefore requires no external support.
One whose manifestation as the universe resembles the blooming (Hāsa) of buds into flowers.
One who is particularly awake – being eternal Awareness itself.
One who is above everything.
One who always follows the conduct of the good.
One who restores life to the dead, as in the case of Parīkṣit.
Praṇava (Oṃ) – the manifesting sound-symbol of Brahman. As He is inseparably related to Praṇava, He is called Praṇava.
From the root meaning transaction – one who bestows the fruits of Karma on all according to their actions.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
प्रमाणं प्राणनिलयः प्राणभृत्प्राणजीवनः ।
तत्त्वं तत्त्वविदेकात्मा जन्ममृत्युजरातिगः ॥१०३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: प्रमाणं प्राणनिलयः प्राणभृत्प्राणजीवनः । | तत्त्वं तत्त्वविदेकात्मा जन्ममृत्युजरातिगः ॥१०३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
pramāṇaṃ prāṇanilayaḥ prāṇabhṛt prāṇajīvanaḥ,
tattvaṃ tattvavid ekātmā janmamṛtyujarātigaḥ. (103)
shlokas.meaning_english: Pramāṇaṃ: One who is self-certifying, being Pure Consciousness.; Prāṇanilayaḥ: The home and dissolving ground of the Prāṇas.; Prāṇa: bhṛt – One who strengthens the Prāṇas as food (Anna) nourishes.; Prāṇa: jīvanaḥ – He who keeps human beings alive through the Vāyus known as Prāṇa, Apāna, etc.; Tattvaṃ: Means Brahman – like words such as Amṛta, Satya, Paramārtha.; Tattvavid: One who knows His own true nature.; Ekātmā: One who is the sole being and the spirit (Ātmā) in all.; Janma: mṛtyu-jarātigaḥ – One who subsists without being subject to the six kinds of transformation – birth, existence, growth, transformation, decay and death.

padas.meaning: One who is self-certifying, being Pure Consciousness.
The home and dissolving ground of the Prāṇas.
bhṛt – One who strengthens the Prāṇas as food (Anna) nourishes.
jīvanaḥ – He who keeps human beings alive through the Vāyus known as Prāṇa, Apāna, etc.
Means Brahman – like words such as Amṛta, Satya, Paramārtha.
One who knows His own true nature.
One who is the sole being and the spirit (Ātmā) in all.
mṛtyu-jarātigaḥ – One who subsists without being subject to the six kinds of transformation – birth, existence, growth, transformation, decay and death.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भूर्भुवःस्वस्तरुस्तारः सविता प्रपितामहः ।
यज्ञो यज्ञपतिर्यज्वा यज्ञाङ्गो यज्ञवाहनः ॥१०४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भूर्भुवःस्वस्तरुस्तारः सविता प्रपितामहः । | यज्ञो यज्ञपतिर्यज्वा यज्ञाङ्गो यज्ञवाहनः ॥१०४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
bhūrbhuvaḥ svastaruḥ tāraḥ savitā prapitāmahaḥ,
yajño yajñapatir yajvā yajñāṅgo yajñavāhanaḥ. (104)
shlokas.meaning_english: Bhūr: bhuvaḥ-svastaruḥ – The three Vyāhṛtis – Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ – are the essence of the Veda; He is the tree (Taru) from which they spring.; Tāraḥ: One who helps Jīvas cross over the ocean of Saṃsāra.; Savitā: He who generates all the worlds.; Prapitāmahaḥ: One who is the father of Brahmā and therefore the grandfather of all.; Yajñaḥ: One who is of the form of Yajña.; Yajñapatiḥ: The protector and master of all Yajñas.; Yajvā: One who manifests as the performer of a Yajña.; Yajñāṅgaḥ: All the parts of His body as the Cosmic Boar are identified with the parts of a Yajña.; Yajña: vāhanaḥ – One who supports the Yajñas which yield various fruits.

padas.meaning: bhuvaḥ-svastaruḥ – The three Vyāhṛtis – Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ – are the essence of the Veda; He is the tree (Taru) from which they spring.
One who helps Jīvas cross over the ocean of Saṃsāra.
He who generates all the worlds.
One who is the father of Brahmā and therefore the grandfather of all.
One who is of the form of Yajña.
The protector and master of all Yajñas.
One who manifests as the performer of a Yajña.
All the parts of His body as the Cosmic Boar are identified with the parts of a Yajña.
vāhanaḥ – One who supports the Yajñas which yield various fruits.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यज्ञभृद् यज्ञकृद् यज्ञी यज्ञभुग् यज्ञसाधनः ।
यज्ञान्तकृद् यज्ञगुह्यमन्नमन्नाद एव च ॥१०५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: यज्ञभृद् यज्ञकृद् यज्ञी यज्ञभुग् यज्ञसाधनः । | यज्ञान्तकृद् यज्ञगुह्यमन्नमन्नाद एव च ॥१०५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yajñabhṛd yajñakṛd yajñī yajñabhug yajñasādhanaḥ,
yajñāntakṛd yajñaguhyam annam annāda eva ca. (105)
shlokas.meaning_english: Yajñabhṛd: One who is the protector and supporter of all Yajñas.; Yajñakṛd: One who performs Yajña at the beginning and end of the world.; Yajñī: One who is the Principal, the Lord of Yajña.; Yajñabhug: One who is the enjoyer and protector of Yajña.; Yajña: sādhanaḥ – One to whom the Yajña is the approach – He is both the means and the end.; Yajñāntakṛd: One who is the end and the fruit of Yajña.; Yajñaguhyam: The Jñāna Yajña (sacrifice of knowledge), which is the esoteric (Guhyam) essence of all Yajñas.; Annam: That which is eaten by living beings; or He who pervades all beings as their sustenance.; Annādaḥ: One who is the eater of the whole world as food. Eva (indeed) is added to show that He is also Anna – the food itself.

padas.meaning: One who is the protector and supporter of all Yajñas.
One who performs Yajña at the beginning and end of the world.
One who is the Principal, the Lord of Yajña.
One who is the enjoyer and protector of Yajña.
sādhanaḥ – One to whom the Yajña is the approach – He is both the means and the end.
One who is the end and the fruit of Yajña.
The Jñāna Yajña (sacrifice of knowledge), which is the esoteric (Guhyam) essence of all Yajñas.
That which is eaten by living beings; or He who pervades all beings as their sustenance.
One who is the eater of the whole world as food. Eva (indeed) is added to show that He is also Anna – the food itself.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
आत्मयोनिः स्वयञ्जातो वैखानः सामगायनः ।
देवकीनन्दनः स्रष्टा क्षितीशः पापनाशनः ॥१०६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: आत्मयोनिः स्वयञ्जातो वैखानः सामगायनः । | देवकीनन्दनः स्रष्टा क्षितीशः पापनाशनः ॥१०६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ātmayoniḥ svayaṃjāto vaikhānaḥ sāmagāyanaḥ,
devakīnandanaḥ sraṣṭā kṣitīśaḥ pāpanāśanaḥ. (106)
shlokas.meaning_english: Ātmayoniḥ: One who is the source of all – there is no material cause other than Himself for the universe.; Svayaṃ: jātaḥ – He is also the instrumental cause – self-born, brought into existence by none other.; Vaikhānaḥ: One who excavated the earth in a unique form (as Varāha, the Cosmic Boar).; Sāmagāyanaḥ: One who recites and is sung through the Sāma chants.; Devakī: nandanaḥ – The son of Devakī in the incarnation as Kṛṣṇa.; Sraṣṭā: The creator of all the worlds.; Kṣitīśaḥ: Master of the world – here denoting Rāma.; Pāpanāśanaḥ: He who destroys the sins of those who adore, meditate upon, remember and sing hymns of praise to Him.

padas.meaning: One who is the source of all – there is no material cause other than Himself for the universe.
jātaḥ – He is also the instrumental cause – self-born, brought into existence by none other.
One who excavated the earth in a unique form (as Varāha, the Cosmic Boar).
One who recites and is sung through the Sāma chants.
nandanaḥ – The son of Devakī in the incarnation as Kṛṣṇa.
The creator of all the worlds.
Master of the world – here denoting Rāma.
He who destroys the sins of those who adore, meditate upon, remember and sing hymns of praise to Him.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
शङ्खभृन्नन्दकी चक्री शार्ङ्गधन्वा गदाधरः ।
रथाङ्गपाणिरक्षोभ्यः सर्वप्रहरणायुधः ॥१०७॥
सर्वप्रहरणायुध ॐ नम इति ।
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: शङ्खभृन्नन्दकी चक्री शार्ङ्गधन्वा गदाधरः । | रथाङ्गपाणिरक्षोभ्यः सर्वप्रहरणायुधः ॥१०७॥ | सर्वप्रहरणायुध ॐ नम इति ।
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śaṅkhabhṛn nandakī cakrī śārṅgadhanvā gadādharaḥ,
rathāṅgapāṇir akṣobhyaḥ sarvapraharaṇāyudhaḥ. (107)
shlokas.meaning_english: Śaṅkhabhṛt: One who bears the conch Pāñcajanya, which stands for Tāmasāhaṃkāra, from which the five elements were born.; Nandakī: One who holds the sword Nandaka, which stands for Vidyā (spiritual illumination).; Cakrī: One who bears the discus Sudarśana, which stands for Rājasāhaṃkāra, from which the Indriyas (senses) have come.; Śārṅga: dhanvā – One who wields the Śārṅga bow.; Gadādharaḥ: One who holds the mace Kaumodakī, which stands for the category of Buddhi (intellect).; Rathāṅga: pāṇiḥ – One in whose hand is a wheel (Cakra).; Akṣobhyaḥ: One who cannot be upset by anything, controlling all the above-mentioned weapons.; Sarva: praharaṇā-yudhaḥ – All things that can be used for contacting or striking are His weapons; His arsenal is unlimited.

padas.meaning: One who bears the conch Pāñcajanya, which stands for Tāmasāhaṃkāra, from which the five elements were born.
One who holds the sword Nandaka, which stands for Vidyā (spiritual illumination).
One who bears the discus Sudarśana, which stands for Rājasāhaṃkāra, from which the Indriyas (senses) have come.
dhanvā – One who wields the Śārṅga bow.
One who holds the mace Kaumodakī, which stands for the category of Buddhi (intellect).
pāṇiḥ – One in whose hand is a wheel (Cakra).
One who cannot be upset by anything, controlling all the above-mentioned weapons.
praharaṇā-yudhaḥ – All things that can be used for contacting or striking are His weapons; His arsenal is unlimited.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वनमाली गदी शार्ङ्गी शङ्खी चक्री च नन्दकी ।
श्रीमान् नारायणो विष्णुर्वासुदेवोऽभिरक्षतु ॥१०८॥
श्री वासुदेवोऽभिरक्षतु ॐ नम इति ।
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: वनमाली गदी शार्ङ्गी शङ्खी चक्री च नन्दकी । | श्रीमान् नारायणो विष्णुर्वासुदेवोऽभिरक्षतु ॥१०८॥ | श्री वासुदेवोऽभिरक्षतु ॐ नम इति ।
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vanamālī gadī śārṅgī śaṅkhī cakrī ca nandakī,
śrīmān nārāyaṇo viṣṇur vāsudevo 'bhirakṣatu. (108)
shlokas.meaning_english: vanamālī: ; gadī: ; śārṅgī: ; śaṅkhī: ; cakrī: ; ca: ; nandakī: ; śrīmān: ; nārāyaṇo: ; viṣṇur: ; vāsudevo: ; 'bhirakṣatu: ; ॐ: ; nama: ; iti:

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच –
इतीदं कीर्तनीयस्य केशवस्य महात्मनः ।
नाम्नां सहस्रं दिव्यानामशेषेण प्रकीर्तितम् ॥१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भीष्म उवाच – | इतीदं कीर्तनीयस्य केशवस्य महात्मनः । | नाम्नां सहस्रं दिव्यानामशेषेण प्रकीर्तितम् ॥१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
bhīṣma uvāca –
itīdaṃ kīrtanīyasya keśavasya mahātmanaḥ,
nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ divyānām aśeṣeṇa prakīrtitam. (1)
shlokas.meaning_english: Bhishma said: Thus, the thousand divine names of the great-souled Kesava, which are worthy of being praised, have been sung in their entirety.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
य इदं शृणुयान्नित्यं यश्चापि परिकीर्तयेत् ।
नाशुभं प्राप्नुयात्किञ्चित्सोऽमुत्रेह च मानवः ॥२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: य इदं शृणुयान्नित्यं यश्चापि परिकीर्तयेत् । | नाशुभं प्राप्नुयात्किञ्चित्सोऽमुत्रेह च मानवः ॥२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ yaś cāpi parikīrtayet,
nāśubhaṃ prāpnuyāt kiñcit so 'mutreha ca mānavaḥ. (2)
shlokas.meaning_english: That man who hears this daily or recites it shall not meet with any evil or inauspiciousness either in this world or in the next.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वेदान्तगो ब्राह्मणः स्यात्क्षत्रियो विजयी भवेत् ।
वैश्यो धनसमृद्धः स्याच्छूद्रः सुखमवाप्नुयात् ॥३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: वेदान्तगो ब्राह्मणः स्यात्क्षत्रियो विजयी भवेत् । | वैश्यो धनसमृद्धः स्याच्छूद्रः सुखमवाप्नुयात् ॥३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vedāntago brāhmaṇaḥ syāt kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet,
vaiśyo dhanasamṛddhaḥ syāc chūdraḥ sukham avāpnuyāt. (3)
shlokas.meaning_english: A Brahmin will attain mastery over the Vedas; a Kshatriya will become victorious; a Vaishya will become wealthy and prosperous; and a Shudra will attain happiness.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
धर्मार्थी प्राप्नुयाद्धर्ममर्थार्थी चार्थमाप्नुयात् ।
कामानवाप्नुयात्कामी प्रजार्थी प्राप्नुयात्प्रजाम् ॥४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: धर्मार्थी प्राप्नुयाद्धर्ममर्थार्थी चार्थमाप्नुयात् । | कामानवाप्नुयात्कामी प्रजार्थी प्राप्नुयात्प्रजाम् ॥४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
dharmārthī prāpnuyād dharmaṃ arthārthī cārtham āpnuyāt,
kāmān avāpnuyāt kāmī prajārthī prāpnuyāt prajām. (4)
shlokas.meaning_english: He who desires righteousness (Dharma) will attain righteousness; he who desires wealth will acquire wealth; he who seeks pleasures will enjoy all pleasures; and he who desires progeny will be blessed with offspring.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
भक्तिमान् यः सदोत्थाय शुचिस्तद्गतमानसः ।
सहस्रं वासुदेवस्य नाम्नामेतत्प्रकीर्तयेत् ॥५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: भक्तिमान् यः सदोत्थाय शुचिस्तद्गतमानसः । | सहस्रं वासुदेवस्य नाम्नामेतत्प्रकीर्तयेत् ॥५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
bhaktimān yaḥ sadotthāya śucis tadgatamānasaḥ,
sahasraṃ vāsudevasya nāmnām etat prakīrtayet. (5)
shlokas.meaning_english: The devoted man who, rising early in the morning and purifying himself, recites these thousand names of Vasudeva with a mind fully absorbed in Him...

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
यशः प्राप्नोोति विपुलं ज्ञातिप्राधान्यमेव च ।
अचलां श्रियमाप्नोोति श्रेयः प्राप्नोोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: यशः प्राप्नोोति विपुलं ज्ञातिप्राधान्यमेव च । | अचलां श्रियमाप्नोोति श्रेयः प्राप्नोोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yaśaḥ prāpnoti vipulaṃ jñātiprādhānyam eva ca,
acalāṃ śriyam āpnoti śreyaḥ prāpnoty anuttamam. (6)
shlokas.meaning_english: ...attains immense fame and leadership among his kinsmen. He acquires steady, unshakeable wealth and achieves the supreme, unsurpassed good.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
न भयं क्वचिदाप्नोोति वीर्यं तेजश्च विन्दति ।
भवत्यरोगो द्युतिमान्बलरूपगुणान्वितः ॥७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: न भयं क्वचिदाप्नोोति वीर्यं तेजश्च विन्दति । | भवत्यरोगो द्युतिमान्बलरूपगुणान्वितः ॥७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
na bhayaṃ kvacid āpnoti vīryaṃ tejaś ca vindati,
bhavaty arogo dyutimān balarūpaguṇānvitaḥ. (7)
shlokas.meaning_english: He never encounters fear from any quarter; he gains exceptional valor and vitality. He remains free from diseases, radiant, and endowed with strength, beauty, and noble virtues.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
रोगार्तो मुच्यते रोगाद्बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात् ।
भयान्मुच्येत भीतस्तु मुच्येतापन्न आपदः ॥८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: रोगार्तो मुच्यते रोगाद्बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात् । | भयान्मुच्येत भीतस्तु मुच्येतापन्न आपदः ॥८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
rogārto mucyate rogād baddho mucyeta bandhanāt,
bhayān mucyeta bhītas tu mucyetāpanna āpadaḥ. (8)
shlokas.meaning_english: One who is afflicted by disease is freed from his sickness; one who is bound is liberated from captivity; one who is terrified is released from fear; and one who is facing a crisis is delivered from adversity.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
दुर्गाण्यतितरत्याशु पुरुषः पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
स्तुवन्नामसहस्रेण नित्यं भक्तिसमन्वितः ॥९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: दुर्गाण्यतितरत्याशु पुरुषः पुरुषोत्तमम् । | स्तुवन्नामसहस्रेण नित्यं भक्तिसमन्वितः ॥९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
durgāṇy atitaraty āśu puruṣaḥ puruṣottamam,
stuvan nāmasahasreṇa nityaṃ bhaktisamanvitaḥ. (9)
shlokas.meaning_english: A man quickly crosses over difficulties by praising the Supreme Person with a thousand names, ever accompanied by devotion.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
वासुदेवाश्रयो मर्त्यो वासुदेवपरायणः ।
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा याति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥१०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: वासुदेवाश्रयो मर्त्यो वासुदेवपरायणः । | सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा याति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥१०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vāsudevāśrayo martyo vāsudevaparāyaṇaḥ,
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā yāti brahma sanātanam. (10)
shlokas.meaning_english: That mortal who takes refuge in Vasudeva and considers Vasudeva as the highest goal becomes completely purified of all sins and attains the eternal Brahman.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
न वासुदेवभक्तानामशुभं विद्यते क्वचित् ।
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिभयं नैवोपजायते ॥११॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: न वासुदेवभक्तानामशुभं विद्यते क्वचित् । | जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिभयं नैवोपजायते ॥११॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
na vāsudevabhaktānām aśubhaṃ vidyate kvacit,
janmamṛtyujarāvyādhibhayaṃ naivopajāyate. (11)
shlokas.meaning_english: There is nothing inauspicious for the devotees of Vāsudeva. They are not afraid of birth, death, old age or disease.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
इमं स्तवमधीयानः श्रद्धाभक्तिसमन्वितः ।
युज्येतात्मसुखक्षान्तिश्रीधृतिस्मृतिकीर्तिभिः ॥१२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: इमं स्तवमधीयानः श्रद्धाभक्तिसमन्वितः । | युज्येतात्मसुखक्षान्तिश्रीधृतिस्मृतिकीर्तिभिः ॥१२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
imaṃ stavam adhīyānaḥ śraddhābhaktisamanvitaḥ,
yujyetātmasukha-kṣānti-śrī-dhṛti-smṛti-kīrtibhiḥ. (12)
shlokas.meaning_english: One who studies this hymn with sincere faith and devotion becomes endowed with inner happiness, forgiveness, prosperity, fortitude, memory, and enduring fame.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
न क्रोोधो न च मात्सर्यं न लोभो नाशुभा मतिः ।
भवन्ति कृतपुण्यानां भक्तानां पुरुषोत्तमे ॥१३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: न क्रोोधो न च मात्सर्यं न लोभो नाशुभा मतिः । | भवन्ति कृतपुण्यानां भक्तानां पुरुषोत्तमे ॥१३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
na krodho na ca mātsaryaṃ na lobho nāśubhā matiḥ,
bhavanti kṛtapuṇyānāṃ bhaktānāṃ puruṣottame. (13)
shlokas.meaning_english: Neither anger, nor malice, nor greed, nor unrighteous thoughts arise in the minds of those highly meritorious devotees who are completely devoted to Purushottama.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
द्यौः सचन्द्राार्कनक्षत्रा खं दिशो भूर्महोदधिः ।
वासुदेवस्य वीर्येण विधृतानि महात्मनः ॥१४॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: द्यौः सचन्द्राार्कनक्षत्रा खं दिशो भूर्महोदधिः । | वासुदेवस्य वीर्येण विधृतानि महात्मनः ॥१४॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
dyauḥ sacandrārkanakṣatrā khaṃ diśo bhūr mahodadhiḥ,
vāsudevasya vīryeṇa vidhṛtāni mahātmanaḥ. (14)
shlokas.meaning_english: The firmament along with the moon, sun, and stars, the sky, the directions, the earth, and the great ocean are all sustained and held together by the supreme power of the high-souled Vasudeva.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ससुरासुरगन्धर्वं सयक्षोरगराक्षसम् ।
जगद्वशे वर्ततेदं कृष्णस्य सचराचरम् ॥१५॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ससुरासुरगन्धर्वं सयक्षोरगराक्षसम् । | जगद्वशे वर्ततेदं कृष्णस्य सचराचरम् ॥१५॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sasurāsuragandharvaṃ sayakṣoragarākṣasam,
jagadvaśe vartate 'daṃ kṛṣṇasya sacarācaram. (15)
shlokas.meaning_english: This entire universe, containing moving and non-moving entities, along with the gods (Devas), demons (Asuras), celestial musicians (Gandharvas), Yakshas, Nagas, and Rakshasas, remains under the absolute control of Lord Krishna.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिः सत्त्वं तेजो बलं धृतिः ।
वासुदेवात्मकान्याहुः क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञ एव च ॥१६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिः सत्त्वं तेजो बलं धृतिः । | वासुदेवात्मकान्याहुः क्षेत्रं क्षेत्रज्ञ एव च ॥१६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
indriyāṇi mano buddhiḥ sattvaṃ tejo balaṃ dhṛtiḥ,
vāsudevātmakāny āhuḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetrajña eva ca. (16)
shlokas.meaning_english: The senses, mind, intellect, being (sattva), splendour, strength, and fortitude, as well as the body (Kshetra) and the individual soul (Kshetrajna), are all declared to have Vasudeva as their inner essence.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सर्वागमानामाचारः प्रथमं परिकल्प्यते ।
आचारप्रभवो धर्मो धर्मस्य प्रभुरच्युतः ॥१७॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सर्वागमानामाचारः प्रथमं परिकल्प्यते । | आचारप्रभवो धर्मो धर्मस्य प्रभुरच्युतः ॥१७॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sarvāgamānām ācāraḥ prathamaṃ parikalpyate,
ācāraprabhavo dharmo dharmasya prabhur acyutaḥ. (17)
shlokas.meaning_english: Conduct (ācāra) is considered the foremost of all āgamas (sacred traditions/scriptures). Righteousness (Dharma) springs from righteous conduct, and Lord Achyuta is the supreme master of all Dharma.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ऋषयः पितरो देवा महाभूतानि धातवः ।
जङ्गमाजङ्गमं चेदं जगन्नारायणोद्भवम् ॥१८॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ऋषयः पितरो देवा महाभूतानि धातवः । | जङ्गमाजङ्गमं चेदं जगन्नारायणोद्भवम् ॥१८॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā mahābhūtāni dhātavaḥ,
jaṅgamājaṅgamaṃ cedaṃ jagan nārāyaṇodbhavam. (18)
shlokas.meaning_english: The celestial sages, the ancestors (Pitrus), the gods, the primordial elements, the bodily constituents, and this entire universe of moving and stationary objects have all originated from Narayana.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
योगो ज्ञानं तथा साङ्ख्यं विद्याः शिल्पादि कर्म च ।
वेदाः शास्त्राणि विज्ञानमेतत्सर्वं जनार्दनात् ॥१९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: योगो ज्ञानं तथा साङ्ख्यं विद्याः शिल्पादि कर्म च । | वेदाः शास्त्राणि विज्ञानमेतत्सर्वं जनार्दनात् ॥१९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
yogo jñānaṃ tathā sāṅkhyaṃ vidyāḥ śilpādi karma ca,
vedāḥ śāstrāṇi vijñānam etat sarvaṃ janārdanāt. (19)
shlokas.meaning_english: Yoga, knowledge (Jnana), the Samkhya philosophy, sciences, arts, crafts, the Vedas, the sacred scriptures, and experiential wisdom—all these emanate from Lord Janardana.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
एको विष्णुर्महद्भूतं पृथग्भूतान्यनेकशः ।
त्रींल्लोकान्व्याप्य भूतात्मा भुङ्क्ते विश्वभुगव्ययः ॥२०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: एको विष्णुर्महद्भूतं पृथग्भूतान्यनेकशः । | त्रींल्लोकान्व्याप्य भूतात्मा भुङ्क्ते विश्वभुगव्ययः ॥२०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
eko viṣṇur mahadbhūtaṃ pṛthagbhūtāny anekaśaḥ,
trīn lokān vyāpya bhūtātmā bhuṅkte viśvabhug avyayaḥ. (20)
shlokas.meaning_english: The one all-pervading Lord Vishnu is the great reality behind all distinct beings. Pervading the three worlds as the inner soul of all, the inexhaustible enjoyer of the universe experiences all creation.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
इमं स्तवं भगवतो विष्णोर्व्यासेन कीर्तितम् ।
पठेद्य इच्छेत्पुरुषः श्रेयः प्राप्तुं सुखानि च ॥२१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: इमं स्तवं भगवतो विष्णोर्व्यासेन कीर्तितम् । | पठेद्य इच्छेत्पुरुषः श्रेयः प्राप्तुं सुखानि च ॥२१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
imaṃ stavaṃ bhagavato viṣṇor vyāsena kīrtitam,
paṭhed ya icchet puruṣaḥ śreyaḥ prāptuṃ sukhāni ca. (21)
shlokas.meaning_english: Any person who desires to attain ultimate welfare, prosperity, and happiness should recite this hymn of Lord Vishnu, composed and sung by Sage Vyasa.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
विश्वेश्वरमजं देवं जगतः प्रभुमव्ययम् ।
भजन्ति ये पुष्कराक्षं न ते यान्ति पराभवम् ॥२२॥
न ते यान्ति पराभवं ॐ नम इति ।
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: विश्वेश्वरमजं देवं जगतः प्रभुमव्ययम् । | भजन्ति ये पुष्कराक्षं न ते यान्ति पराभवम् ॥२२॥ | न ते यान्ति पराभवं ॐ नम इति ।
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
viśveśvaram ajaṃ devaṃ jagataḥ prabhavāpyayam,
bhajanti ye puṣkarākṣaṃ na te yānti parābhavam. (22)
shlokas.meaning_english: na te yānti parābhavam oṃ nama iti. Those who worship the lotus-eyed, unborn Lord of the universe, who is the source and dissolution of everything and who is inexhaustible, never encounter defeat or humiliation. They never encounter defeat. Om Namah.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच –
पद्मपत्रविशालाक्ष पद्मनाभ सुरोत्तम ।
भक्तानामनुरक्तानां त्राता भव जनार्दन ॥२३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच – | पद्मपत्रविशालाक्ष पद्मनाभ सुरोत्तम । | भक्तानामनुरक्तानां त्राता भव जनार्दन ॥२३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
arjuna uvāca –
padmapatraviśālākṣa padmanābha surottama,
bhaktānām anuraktānāṃ trātā bhava janārdana. (23)
shlokas.meaning_english: Arjuna said: O Lord with large eyes like lotus petals, O Padmanabha (He from whose navel the lotus emerges), O best of gods! Be the savior of Your deeply attached and loving devotees, O Janardana.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच –
यो मां नामसहस्रेण स्तोतुमिच्छति पाण्डव ।
सोऽहमेकेन श्लोोकेन स्तुत एव न संशयः ॥२४॥
(स्तुत एव न संशय ॐ नम इति ।)
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच – | यो मां नामसहस्रेण स्तोतुमिच्छति पाण्डव । | सोऽहमेकेन श्लोोकेन स्तुत एव न संशयः ॥२४॥ | (स्तुत एव न संशय ॐ नम इति ।)
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śrī bhagavān uvāca –
yo māṃ nāmasahasreṇa stotum icchati pāṇḍava,
so 'ham ekena ślokena stuta eva na saṃśayaḥ. (24)
shlokas.meaning_english: (stuta eva na saṃśaya oṃ nama iti.) The Blessed Lord (Śrī Bhagavān) said: O Arjuna (son of Pandu)! If someone desires to praise Me with the full thousand names, let him know that I am equally pleased and praised by the recitation of just a single stanza. There is absolutely no doubt about this.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
व्यास उवाच –
वासनाद्वासुदेवस्य वासितं भुवनत्रयम् ।
सर्वभूतनिवासोऽसि वासुदेव नमोऽस्तु ते ॥२५॥
(श्री वासुदेव नमोऽस्तुत ॐ नम इति ।)
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: व्यास उवाच – | वासनाद्वासुदेवस्य वासितं भुवनत्रयम् । | सर्वभूतनिवासोऽसि वासुदेव नमोऽस्तु ते ॥२५॥ | (श्री वासुदेव नमोऽस्तुत ॐ नम इति ।)
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
vyāsa uvāca –
vāsanād vāsudevasya vāsitaṃ bhuvanatrayam,
sarvabhūtanivāso 'si vāsudeva namo 'stu te. (25)
shlokas.meaning_english: (śrī vāsudeva namo 'stu te oṃ nama iti.) Sage Vyasa said: Because Vāsudeva pervades everything, the three worlds are permeated by Him. You are the dwelling place of all living beings – O Vāsudeva, salutations to You.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
पार्वत्युवाच –
केनोपायेन लघुना विष्णोर्नामसहस्रकम् ।
पठ्यते पण्डितैर्नित्यं श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं प्रभो ॥२६॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: पार्वत्युवाच – | केनोपायेन लघुना विष्णोर्नामसहस्रकम् । | पठ्यते पण्डितैर्नित्यं श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं प्रभो ॥२६॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
pārvatyuvāca –
kenopāyena laghunā viṣṇor nāmasahasrakam,
paṭhyate paṇḍitair nityaṃ śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ prabho. (26)
shlokas.meaning_english: Goddess Parvati said: O Lord, I wish to hear how the learned scholars daily recite these thousand names of Lord Vishnu by some brief and easy method.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ईश्वर उवाच –
श्रीराम राम रामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे ।
सहस्रनाम तत्तुल्यं रामनाम वरानने ॥२७॥
(श्रीरामनाम वरानन ॐ नम इति ।)
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच – | श्रीराम राम रामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे । | सहस्रनाम तत्तुल्यं रामनाम वरानने ॥२७॥ | (श्रीरामनाम वरानन ॐ नम इति ।)
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
īśvara uvāca –
śrīrāma rāma rāmeti rame rāme manorame,
sahasranāma tat tulyaṃ rāmanāma varānane. (27)
shlokas.meaning_english: (śrīrāmanāma varānane oṃ nama iti.) Lord Shiva (Ishvara) replied: O beautiful-faced one! I delight in chanting the sweet name of 'Rama, Rama, Rama,' which gladdens the mind. Chanting the single holy name of 'Rama' is completely equivalent to reciting the entire thousand names of Lord Vishnu.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
ब्रह्मोवाच –
नमोऽस्त्वनन्ताय सहस्रमूर्तये सहस्रपादाक्षिशिरोरुबाहवे ।
सहस्रनाम्ने पुरुषाय शाश्वते सहस्रकोटियुगधारिणे नमः ॥२८॥
(सहस्रकोटियुगधारिणे ॐ नम इति ।)
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: ब्रह्मोवाच – | नमोऽस्त्वनन्ताय सहस्रमूर्तये सहस्रपादाक्षिशिरोरुबाहवे । | सहस्रनाम्ने पुरुषाय शाश्वते सहस्रकोटियुगधारिणे नमः ॥२८॥ | (सहस्रकोटियुगधारिणे ॐ नम इति ।)
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
brahmo vāca –
namo 'stv anantāya sahasramūrtaye sahasrapādākṣiśirorubāhave,
sahasranāmne puruṣāya śāśvate sahasrakoṭiyugadhāriṇe namaḥ.
(28)
shlokas.meaning_english: (sahasrakoṭiyugadhāriṇe oṃ nama iti.) Lord Brahma said: Salutations to the Infinite Being, who possesses thousands of cosmic forms, thousands of feet, eyes, heads, thighs, and arms. Salutations to the eternal Supreme Person who is praised by a thousand names, and who upholds countless cosmic cycles.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच –
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥२९॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: सञ्जय उवाच – | यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः । | तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥२९॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
sañjaya uvāca –
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ,
tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama. (29)
shlokas.meaning_english: Sanjaya said: Wherever there is Krishna, the supreme Lord of Yoga, and wherever there is Arjuna, the wielder of the bow, there will certainly be opulence, victory, extraordinary prosperity, and unswerving righteousness. This is my firm conviction.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच –
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते ।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥३०॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच – | अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥३०॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
śrī bhagavān uvāca –
ananyāś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate,
teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmy aham. (30)
shlokas.meaning_english: The Supreme Lord said: For those people who worship Me with undivided devotion, meditating exclusively on Me, and who are perpetually attuned to Me, I personally carry and secure their spiritual and material welfare (Yoga and Kshema).

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥३१॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । | धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥३१॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām,
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge. (31)
shlokas.meaning_english: For the protection of the righteous, the total destruction of the wicked, and for the firm re-establishment of righteousness, I manifest myself age after age.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
आर्ताः विषण्णाः शिथिलाश्च भीताः घोरेषु च व्याधिषु वर्तमानाः ।
सङ्कीर्त्य नारायणशब्दमात्रं विमुक्तदुःखाः सुखिनो भवन्ति ॥३२॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: आर्ताः विषण्णाः शिथिलाश्च भीताः घोरेषु च व्याधिषु वर्तमानाः । | सङ्कीर्त्य नारायणशब्दमात्रं विमुक्तदुःखाः सुखिनो भवन्ति ॥३२॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
ārtā viṣaṇṇāḥ śithilāś ca bhītāḥ ghoreṣu ca vyādhiṣu vartamānāḥ,
saṅkīrtya nārāyaṇaśabdamātraṃ vimuktaduḥkhāḥ sukhino bhavanti.
(32)
shlokas.meaning_english: Those who are distressed, deeply dejected, physically broken, terrified, or suffering from horrific, painful diseases, become completely liberated from their suffering and attain supreme happiness by merely chanting the sacred name 'Nārāyaṇa'.

shlokas.full_sanskrit:
कायेन वाचा मनसेन्द्रियैर्वा बुद्ध्याात्मना वा प्रकृतेः स्वभावात् ।
करोमि यद्यत् सकलं परस्मै नारायणायेति समर्पयामि ॥३३॥
shlokas.sandhi_split_sanskrit: कायेन वाचा मनसेन्द्रियैर्वा बुद्ध्याात्मना वा प्रकृतेः स्वभावात् । | करोमि यद्यत् सकलं परस्मै नारायणायेति समर्पयामि ॥३३॥
shlokas.iast_transliteration:
kāyena vācā manasendriyair vā buddhyātmanā vā prakṛteḥ
svabhāvāt,
karomi yad yat sakalaṃ parasmai nārāyaṇāyeti samarpayāmi. (33)
shlokas.meaning_english: Whatever actions I perform with my body, speech, mind, senses, intellect, soul, or driven by my innate nature, I offer all of it to the Supreme (Nārāyaṇa).
